sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level and the internal assessments that follow
paragraphs: Subject choice in the Diploma Programme is made once and lived with for two years, and the most common regret we hear is not a subject that was too hard. It is a Higher Level chosen for a university application that the student had already stopped wanting. Three Higher Level subjects carry three sets of coursework and the deepest content, so the useful test is whether the student would read around that subject without being told to. A tutor can rescue a difficult Higher Level choice; they cannot manufacture interest that was never there.

The internal assessments are where a tutor earns their fee. Every Diploma Programme subject carries one, and they are marked against criteria that are published, specific and almost never read by the student. The sciences require an investigation with a defensible research question, controlled variables and real uncertainty analysis. Mathematics requires an exploration where the mathematics has to be genuinely used rather than described. Languages and humanities carry written tasks with their own command terms. The sibling pages on this site handle individual subjects in depth; what matters for a general enquiry is that the tutor has read the criteria for your child's subject, not a summary of them.

The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are the two components families underestimate most, and they collide. Sequencing those deadlines is ordinary project management and is entirely teachable, which is why we ask for the school's deadline sheet at the first session.

Younger students need something different from the same tutor pool. A Middle Years student does not need coursework strategy; they need to learn to write an explanation that a marker can follow. A Primary Years child needs to stop guessing at words and start decoding them. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Worli Sea Face families book tend to start from exactly one of those three problems, and naming which one you have in the enquiry saves a fortnight of discovery.

Prabhadevi is the nearest station and the reference point for anyone travelling by train. Metro Line 3 on the Aqua corridor between Cuffe Parade and BKC has genuinely changed which cross-city matches are viable, because a tutor who used to be an hour away by road may now be thirty-five minutes away underground. A tutor living there can reach Worli Sea Face, Prabhadevi and Lower Parel within the same short radius, which means they can stack three students across one evening instead of one. That stacking is what makes a 7.30pm slot possible at all, since a tutor travelling for a single lesson will always prefer the earlier time that every other family on the sea face also wants.

There is a version of this calculation that families get wrong in the opposite direction. Choosing a tutor purely because they live in the next building, when they have never taught your child's programme stage, buys three months of convenient sessions that achieve nothing. Proximity is a constraint, not a qualification. We treat it as the tie-breaker between candidates who can both teach the stage, and we will tell you plainly when the only genuinely qualified option for a scarce Higher Level subject lives further out and the slot will therefore need to be earlier.

The shape of the year is reasonably consistent across International Baccalaureate schools in Mumbai. The stretch from October to early December is where Diploma Programme coursework drafts, mock examinations and Middle Years summative tasks overlap, and it is when demand for evening home classes on this corridor peaks. Primary Years families run on a different clock and are often caught out by it. The Grade 5 exhibition arrives in the second half of the year and is the first time many children are asked to drive a piece of extended independent work. The practical advice from all of this is to call before the calendar makes the decision for you. A family enquiring in late October on this corridor is bidding for the same two slots as every neighbour, and is asking a tutor to fix in six weeks what took a year to build. sections.heading: Home tuition first, then online: the honest comparison
paragraphs: Home tuition leads on this page because the Diploma Programme problems that bring parents here are mostly visible only in person. A student who cannot define a research question will talk fluently about their topic on a video call and then write three pages of description. Sitting beside them, a tutor sees the moment the pen hesitates, the paragraph that gets deleted, the diagram drawn without axes. IB home tuition in Worli Sea Face is also simply easier to sustain here than anywhere else in the city, because once a standing gate pass exists the weekly logistics cost nothing.

An IB online tutor in Worli Sea Face is the right call in three situations. A scarce Higher Level subject where the only genuinely experienced teacher is in another city. The weeks immediately before an examination session, when three short contacts beat one long one. And any arrangement that has to survive monsoon disruption, family travel or a week of illness without collapsing. Online also handles document work well: an Extended Essay draft on a shared screen with comments in the margin is often better than two heads over one printed copy.

The costs of going online are real and worth stating. Younger students leak attention within fifteen minutes unless an adult is nearby. Mathematics and the sciences slow down badly when every diagram has to be drawn with a mouse or a tablet pen. And a tutor who has never been in the room has no idea whether the student's study space is usable, which matters more than parents expect; a desk facing a television defeats most teaching.

Hybrid is where most families on this corridor end up. One weekly home session as the anchor, where diagnosis and technique happen face to face, plus a short online contact for a specific topic, a draft review or a paper walkthrough. As an examination session approaches the balance tilts online, because frequency starts to matter more than presence. The home classes stay in place as the fixed point, and the standing building pass means the weekly home tutoring can shift back and forth online without any administration at all.

sections.heading: What is checked before an IB home tutor in Worli Sea Face reaches your door?
paragraphs: Three things are verified and it is worth being precise about which. Identity, through government photo identification matched to the person who turns up. Qualification, meaning the degree or teaching credential exists and is in the subject claimed. And programme experience, which is the one that matters most and is checked hardest: a tutor claiming Diploma Programme Chemistry has to be able to describe the Internal Assessment criteria and what distinguishes a weak research question from a strong one. Adjacent experience is not the same thing, and we do not let a profile blur a national-board teaching history into International Baccalaureate experience.

Verification stops short of fit, and it always will. A tutor can clear every check and still be the wrong person for a particular fourteen-year-old who has decided they do not want help. This is why there is a parent call before confirmation and why the first paid session is diagnostic rather than instructional. Deciding whether this person can hold your child's attention across a long Mumbai evening is a judgement nobody can make on your behalf, and it is cheaper to make it in week one.

Your own checks are short and they are the ones that catch problems. Ask the tutor to describe the assessment components for your child's exact subject and stage, and treat vagueness as disqualifying rather than modest. Ask what the first session will consist of, and listen for whether it involves reading the student's own marked work. Ask what you will receive after four weeks. Be wary of anyone who answers that question with a promised grade instead of a plan, because IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor offers one either.

Building clearance is the last check and the one specific to this corridor. Worli Sea Face is a line of sea-facing towers with strict visitor registration, so tutors here are given a standing gate pass rather than being cleared session by session. In practice that means you lodge the tutor's identity details with the building office once, in the first week, and every subsequent visit is a signature against a standing entry. Towers such as Omkar 1973 and Piramal Aranya keep the pass list at the lobby desk. Families who leave this undone spend a tenth of every paid session waiting downstairs.

sections.heading: Why proximity beats reputation for a weekly slot in Mumbai
paragraphs: The hard version of this page's argument is that for a year-long arrangement, the nearer competent tutor usually outperforms the further excellent one, and the reason is attendance. Fifty scheduled sessions at a realistic ninety per cent attendance gives forty-five lessons. The same fifty at seventy per cent, which is what a cross-city evening commute produces by February, gives thirty-five. Ten lessons is most of a term. No difference in teaching quality between two qualified tutors is large enough to recover ten missing lessons, which is why an IB tutor near me in Worli Sea Face is not a lazy search. It is the correct search.

Attendance decays in a predictable pattern and it helps to know the shape. The first month is near perfect because everyone is motivated. Weeks five to eight produce the first cancellation, usually the tutor's, usually traffic. By week twelve a long commute has generated a request to shift the slot later or move it to the weekend, and weekend slots compete with family time and lose. By the second term the arrangement has either become local or it has become fortnightly. Matching inside the island is the way to avoid walking that path at all.

The exception is genuine scarcity, and we do not pretend it away. For a less common Higher Level subject, or a Diploma Programme language beyond the usual three, the pool inside South Mumbai may contain nobody with real programme experience. In that case the honest options are an earlier weekday slot so the tutor travels against the peak, a weekend home session, or a strong online specialist. What we will not do is put a generalist in the chair because they live nearby and let you discover the gap in January.

There is a related trap in how parents read tutor reputation. A tutor described as the best IB tutor in Worli Sea Face by one family may simply have been a good fit for a different child at a different stage. A recommendation is evidence about one match, not a ranking, and it is worth almost nothing without knowing the subject, the stage and what problem was being solved. The two questions that actually transfer are whether the tutor turned up reliably and whether the parent could see, after a month, what had changed.

sections.heading: What does progress look like at four weeks and at one term?
paragraphs: At four weeks you are looking for changed working habits, and the markers are concrete enough to check yourself. The student starts a question without asking whether they are allowed to. They attempt the parts of a paper they used to leave blank. They can restate what a task is asking before attempting it. They bring their own list of confusions to the session instead of waiting to be tested. Two of those four at four weeks is normal. None of them is a signal to have a direct conversation with the tutor, and we would rather you had it then than in March.

At one term the change should be visible in school work, not only in the sessions. A Diploma Programme student should have a research question their teacher has accepted, or a draft that came back with comments about refinement rather than about starting again. A Middle Years student should have moved up a level in at least one criterion and should be able to say which one and why. A Primary Years child should be reading something longer than they were in June. The tutor should be able to name the secure topics and the weak ones. A report that says things are going well is not a report.

Across a full examination cycle the honest claim is narrower than most advertising suggests. A good match closes the gap between what a student knows and what they produce under timed conditions, and that gap is often substantial. It does not change how much the student knows in subjects they are not being tutored in, how well the school teaches, or how much work the student is willing to do. IB Gram publishes no success rates and does not guarantee grades, and any platform that does either is describing marketing rather than outcomes.

Some enquiries should end without a booking and we try to say so. A student who is behind in six subjects at once has a problem tuition in one subject will not touch, and the first conversation belongs with the school. A student who is coping fine and whose parents want insurance will usually resent the hour. A Middle Years student who has been told a tutor is the consequence of a bad report arrives having already decided to waste your money. IB tuition fees in Worli Sea Face are not trivial, and spending them on an unwilling student is the most common way they are wasted.

sections.heading: Does the programme stage change how near a tutor needs to be?
paragraphs: Considerably. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child needs short, frequent, low-friction contact, which means the tutor has to be genuinely close or the arrangement will not survive a month. Thirty-five minutes of reading practice is not worth a fifty-minute journey to anybody, and the tutor will start asking to consolidate two sessions into one long one that a seven-year-old cannot use. For the youngest students, proximity is not a convenience; it is a condition of the thing working at all.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) sits in the middle. Criteria A to D assessment means the work comes in tasks spread across the year rather than in one examination run, so a weekly session of reasonable length suits it well and a tutor twenty-five minutes away is perfectly viable. What a nearby tutor adds at this stage is the ability to slot in an extra hour when a criterion-based task lands with a week's notice, which happens often in MYP and almost never fits neatly into a fixed weekly rhythm.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is where families are most tempted to trade distance for expertise, and where the trade is most defensible. A DP2 student needs someone who has read a lot of Internal Assessment (IA) drafts in that specific subject, has a view on Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay structure, and knows what an examiner rewards in a Higher Level paper. If that person lives in Juhu rather than Prabhadevi, it may still be the right call, because the expertise gap is doing more damage than the travel will. What we will not do is pretend the travel is free. A tutor crossing from the suburbs for a 6.30pm DP slot will cancel sometimes, and you should plan for that rather than discover it.

The stage also changes what a missed session costs. A missed PYP hour is a minor annoyance. A missed DP2 hour in the fortnight before an IA deadline is a real loss, which is why we weight travel reliability more heavily as the stage rises, not less. Families who want an IB private tutor Worli households keep for two years should be asking about the tutor's journey in detail, not politely skipping over it. The home tuition arrangements that last longest in Mumbai are the ones where nobody has to be heroic about traffic.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects can tolerate a tutor who lives further away?
paragraphs: The ones that are mostly written work and mostly discussion. A Higher Level English or Economics student who needs their essay structure taken apart can do a great deal of that over a screen, and a strong specialist forty minutes away is a reasonable arrangement if you accept that one or two sessions a term will move online. TOK is the clearest case of all: it is an argument subject, the work is textual, and the best person for it may well be nowhere near Worli. Theory of Knowledge is where we most often advise a family to stop optimising for distance.

The subjects that punish distance are the ones where a tutor needs to watch a hand move. Mathematics at both levels, the quantitative parts of Physics and Chemistry, and anything where marks are lost in layout rather than in understanding, all depend on somebody sitting beside the page catching a skipped line of working in the three seconds where catching it matters. A photograph of the finished attempt, sent afterwards, shows you the result but not the decision. For these, a nearby tutor is worth more than a marginally better distant one, and all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Worli families book tend to start with exactly these.

Then there is the scarcity case, which overrides both of the above. If your child is taking a less commonly offered Group 2 language, or a Higher Level subject with few teachers in the city, the right specialist may simply not live within reach. Here the choice is not between near and far but between a well-matched remote tutor and a poorly matched local one, and the remote tutor wins almost every time. We would rather tell you that plainly than send you a nearby profile who will be learning the subject alongside your child.

The practical answer for most households is to split the week by subject type rather than by convenience. Keep the mathematical or technical subject in person with somebody close, and run the written or discursive subject online with whoever is genuinely best at it. sections.heading: Fifteen minutes from Bandra, forty from Colaba: the Worli map rewritten
paragraphs: The fact that makes this corridor unusual is the Sea Link ramp. Because the Bandra–Worli Sea Link lands traffic almost at the corridor, a tutor living in Bandra reaches Worli in about fifteen minutes outside peak hours, which makes Worli the most readily accepted cross-bay tutor match in Mumbai. Suburban tutors who will not consider Nepean Sea Road or Cuffe Parade will take a Worli slot without argument. The consequence is that your effective catchment is not a circle around your building; it is a lopsided shape stretching north across the bay and barely reaching south down the island.

Southward is the direction that disappoints people. South Mumbai is dense and short in distance but slow, and a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers roughly eight kilometres and can still lose a large part of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. A parent who assumes a Colaba-based tutor is closer than a Khar-based one is working from the map rather than from the clock. We match within the island where we can, but the island is not uniformly near, and the signals are the reason.

Inside the immediate radius, a tutor working here will usually also hold slots on Worli Sea Face, in Prabhadevi and in Lower Parel. These are the addresses within a few minutes of each other off-peak, which means a tutor can run two sessions in one evening and will therefore accept a slot that would otherwise be uneconomic. It also means the early evening hour in your building is often already taken by a household a few hundred metres away, and asking for 7.15pm rather than waiting for 6pm to free up is the faster route to a tutor. Almost all the home tuition we arrange across this part of Mumbai is built around that two-stop evening.

On public transport, the nearest railway stations are Prabhadevi / Mahalaxmi on the Western Line that runs up from Churchgate through Grant Road and Mumbai Central, and this is a bigger deal than it sounds. A tutor who commutes by train has a predictable journey in a city where road times are not, so train-reachable addresses get more reliable attendance. The Harbour Line through CSMT, Dockyard and Sewri serves the eastern side of the island, Metro Line 3 (Aqua) along the Cuffe Parade to BKC alignment has brought BKC-side tutors into range, and the Coastal Road helps on the western edge. If you live in Omkar 1973, Indiabulls Blu or Lodha World Towers, add the gate: ten minutes of queueing at a single visitor entrance is part of the journey too.

sections.heading: School pick-up, the Mumbai evening, and why 6pm is the hardest slot
paragraphs: Every family wants the same hour and it is the one hour that does not work. The 6pm slot collides with school pick-up traffic, with the start of the office exodus from Lower Parel, and with the window in which a child has just got home and has not eaten. Tutors know this, which is why a 6pm request produces a thin shortlist and a 7.15pm or 7.30pm request produces a healthy one. If your household can shift the hour by seventy-five minutes you will get a meaningfully better-matched tutor, and that is a better trade than most parents realise they are being offered.

The school calendar then decides when the hour matters most. Children on this corridor commonly attend Ryan Global School, Aditya Birla World Academy and JBCN International School, Parel, among others, and each runs its own internal assessment rounds on top of the IB requirements. We name them as local context; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them and no tutor should imply otherwise. The pattern across these schools is consistent enough to plan around: the year opens in June, the first serious assessments land by late July, coursework drafts and mocks fill September to November, and the stretch from November into January is where everything collides.

That collision is the argument for proximity in its strongest form. In November a DP2 student may have an IA draft, a mock paper and a TOK deadline inside the same fortnight, and what helps is not a longer session but an extra one at short notice. A tutor fifteen minutes away can do that. A tutor an hour away cannot, however good they are, because the ask is a two-hour commitment of their evening for a one-hour session. Families who understand this hire for the November they will have rather than for the September they are in.

The monsoon runs across the opening months and is the commonest cause of lost hours here. From June into September a weekday evening visit is genuinely vulnerable, and the households that lose fewest sessions are the ones who settle the rule in week one: a bad road means the session moves online that evening rather than being cancelled. A nearby tutor is less exposed to this, which is one more quiet argument for the shorter journey. Searches like IB tutors near me Worli are, underneath, searches for a slot that survives July.

sections.heading: When home tuition in Worli beats the closest available option
paragraphs: When the closest available option is not qualified for the level, which happens more often than the phrase near me implies. Home tuition is IB Gram's lead service and the home classes we arrange in Mumbai are the default, but the point of the service is a matched tutor who comes to you, not simply a tutor who lives nearby. If the nearest person taught Standard Level Biology last year and your child needs Higher Level Chemistry now, the five-minute walk is not a benefit, it is a distraction from the actual decision. An IB home tutor near me in Worli is worth hiring when both halves of the phrase are satisfied.

In-person teaching earns its place for a reason that has nothing to do with convenience. A tutor at your table sees the pencil stop, sees the student write one line and wait to be rescued, and intervenes in the moment where intervention changes a habit. That signal arrives late or not at all through a camera. For younger students, and for anyone whose real problem is working habits rather than content, this is not a preference between two equivalent options. It is the difference between tutoring that changes behaviour and tutoring that reviews it afterwards.

Online is the right answer in three cases and should be offered without embarrassment. Scarcity, where the specialist for a rare subject or level simply does not live within reach of South Mumbai. Frequency, where two short online contacts a week are practical and two visits are not. And examination season, when students often want brief, repeated contact rather than one long block. An IB online tutor in Worli is a legitimate first choice for an organised DP2 student working on written components, and parents should stop treating it as the compromise.

Hybrid is where most families on this corridor settle, usually by the second term, and it works better when it is designed than when it is drifted into. One in-person session carries the teaching and the relationship; one shorter online session carries the marked work, the follow-up and the question that came up in school on Wednesday. Through the November to January crunch many households invert the ratio for six weeks and then return to it. Nobody should be asked to commit to a single mode for the year during the first week.

sections.heading: How do you check a tutor you found simply because they were close?
paragraphs: With the same three questions you would ask somebody who lived an hour away, and with one extra. Ask which exact level and programme stage they have taught most recently and to how many students, because recency matters more than total experience. Ask what session one will consist of, and listen for whether the answer is diagnostic or a plan to start at the beginning of the syllabus. Ask what evidence they will show you at four weeks. Then ask the extra question: what else is in your Tuesday evening, because a tutor with two other sessions on the corridor is reliable, while one with a session in Andheri at 8.30pm will be watching the clock in your flat.

On our side, verification happens before a profile reaches your shortlist. We check identity and qualifications, and we question the teaching claim rather than accepting a form, so a profile offering all sciences across both boards gets interrogated. We also check the travel claim specifically on this corridor, because a tutor promising 6pm in Worli from a home in Mulund is depending on the Eastern Express Highway behaving in a way it does not. None of that tells you whether the person suits your child, which is what the free discovery call is for and why we never place somebody you have not spoken to.

Some claims should end the conversation. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because the examinations are marked externally and the work is done by your child, so no honest teacher can promise the outcome. Be equally cautious of anyone who claims a relationship with a named school, offers materials they should not have, quotes the grade your child will reach, or asks for a long prepayment before a single lesson. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rates, because any platform quoting one is quoting its best cases.

Finally, verify the thing that nearness was supposed to buy. Ask the tutor directly how many sessions they expect to miss in a year and what happens when they do. A straight answer is a good sign; a claim of never missing one is not credible in Mumbai. The useful commitment is not perfect attendance but a rule you both agree to in advance, usually that a missed evening moves online or is made up within the same week.

sections.heading: The three radii that decide what a nearby tutor can actually do
paragraphs: Think in three bands rather than in kilometres. The first is the walking band: a tutor who lives in your complex or within a few hundred metres, which in practice means someone already teaching on Worli Sea Face or in the next tower along the corridor. This band buys something no other band can, which is the twenty-minute session. A short, unscheduled visit to look at one problem the day before a test is only possible when the journey is trivial, and for a student who panics rather than one who is behind, that is the single most valuable form of help available.

The second band is roughly fifteen to twenty-five minutes, which from Worli covers Prabhadevi, Lower Parel, Mahalaxmi, Dadar and, because of the Sea Link ramp, a good deal of Bandra and Khar. This band supports two sessions a week comfortably and an extra session at short notice when a deadline moves. Most successful arrangements on this corridor sit here. It is also the band where a tutor's cancellation rate stays low enough that you do not lose a working rhythm, which matters more across a term than any single session does.

The third band is forty minutes and beyond, which includes much of the island southwards and most of the central and eastern suburbs. This band supports one weekly session and nothing more. It can be exactly right when the expertise is genuinely scarce, and it is a poor choice when the subject is common, because you are paying a reliability cost for nothing. The mistake to avoid is sitting in band three by accident, having hired on a map, and then wondering why the frequency you planned never materialised.

The reason the bands matter is that frequency, not session length, is what moves work. Two forty-minute contacts in a week beat one eighty-minute session for almost every student, because the second contact catches the misunderstanding before a week of practice embeds it. That is an argument about geography dressed up as an argument about pedagogy. Parents searching best IB tutor in Worli are usually looking for teaching quality, which is reasonable, but the thing that most often separates a working arrangement from a failed one is whether the tutor is close enough to be seen twice.

sections.heading: What a nearby IB home tutor in Worli should deliver by week four
paragraphs: Three things, and none of them is a grade. Four weeks of IB home tuition in Worli is long enough to produce evidence and too short to produce results, so judge the evidence. First, a diagnosis you can repeat: by week two the tutor should have told you in one sentence what the actual weakness is, and by week four the evidence should support it. Second, a visible behaviour change, which for most students is attempting a question before asking for help. Third, proof that the proximity is being used. If your tutor lives fifteen minutes away and you are still on exactly one rigid weekly hour with nothing added in a busy week, you are paying for closeness and not spending it.

At one term the measure moves to the school's own assessments, and the honest pattern is uneven. The weakest component usually improves first while the headline grade lags behind it by a reporting cycle, so a static grade is not evidence of failure if the underlying work has clearly shifted. Ask for the component breakdown rather than the aggregate. A tutor who predicted which component would move first, in writing, in week two, has earned a good deal of credibility by the time it does.

Across a full examination cycle the realistic claim is narrow and worth stating. Tutoring reliably removes avoidable losses: misread questions, missing working, units dropped, later parts of long questions left blank, coursework handed in without a second draft. It reliably builds the fluency that makes a timed paper survivable. It does not reliably rescue content that was never learned, and it cannot undo a Higher Level choice that never suited the student. We do not guarantee grades and we publish no success rates, and any platform that does is showing you its best cases.

When the match is wrong, the fix is quick. Tell us and we replace the tutor from the same shortlist, usually within a few days because the catchment around Worli is reasonably deep, with no lock-in and no notice period. Before switching, separate two situations: a tutor teaching badly, and a competent tutor working with a child who has not agreed to be taught. The second does not improve with a new face. What do IB tuition fees in Worli buy in that situation is a fair question, and the honest answer is a diagnosis you can act on, which is worth having even if the tutoring then stops.

sections.heading: Starting IB home classes in Worli, Mumbai this week
paragraphs: Four things make the first conversation useful. The programme stage written plainly, as MYP Year 9 or DP1 rather than as class ten. The subject and whether it is Higher Level or Standard Level, which changes the shortlist entirely. Two photographs of recent marked work, one strong and one weak, because the contrast tells a tutor more than either on its own. And the hour, stated as a window rather than a point, with 7.15pm or later if your household can manage it, since that single decision widens your shortlist more than anything else you can do.

We then filter verified tutors on stage and level, check who can genuinely hold your window on this corridor through a full term, and send you two or three profiles with their journeys stated honestly. You pick one and speak to them on a free discovery call, where the tutor should ask you more questions than you ask them. Teaching begins after that call. Nothing is payable until you have met the person, and an IB tutor Mumbai parents have never spoken to should never be the one who turns up at the gate.

Session one should be diagnostic rather than instructional. Expect the tutor to work through the papers you sent, set one short unseen question to see where the method breaks rather than where the knowledge stops, ask your child which topics they avoid, and then write you three or four lines naming the gap, the plan for the month and what you should see by week four. If the first hour is a tour of the syllabus, raise it immediately rather than hoping the second hour is better.

From there it is weekly sessions with a short written note each time and a fuller review every two to four weeks. Many households add a shorter online contact from November, and a nearby tutor can usually add an extra hour in the fortnight before a coursework deadline, which is the whole point of hiring nearby. There is no lock-in, no notice period and no minimum term. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope exists does not, so we place one well-matched specialist rather than promising to cover everything.

faqs.question: How near does an IB tutor near me in Worli actually need to live?
faqs.answer: Close enough to be seen twice in a week, which on this corridor means roughly fifteen to twenty-five minutes. That band covers Prabhadevi, Lower Parel, Mahalaxmi, Dadar and, thanks to the Bandra–Worli Sea Link ramp, much of Bandra and Khar. Inside it a tutor can hold two sessions a week and add an hour at short notice before a deadline. Beyond about forty minutes you are buying one weekly session and nothing else, which is the right choice only when the subject expertise is genuinely scarce. An IB tutor near me in Worli is worth the search precisely because this band is unusually wide here, and most of the IB home tuition in Worli that lasts a full year sits inside it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building on the Worli corridor for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and 7pm is a much easier ask than 6pm. The 6pm hour collides with school pick-up traffic and the office exodus from Lower Parel, so it produces a thin shortlist. By 7pm the roads have thinned and a tutor coming from Bandra or Khar across the Sea Link is comfortably inside fifteen to twenty minutes. Give us a window rather than a fixed minute, say 7pm to 7.30pm, and the number of tutors who can take you roughly doubles. The slot you get that way is also the one that survives the whole year.

faqs.question: How does the gate pass work for a weekly tutor at Indiabulls Blu or Lodha World Towers?
faqs.answer: Ask the society office in your first week for a standing weekly visitor entry, requested in writing by the flat owner rather than by the tutor. Large Worli towers with several wings and one visitor gate mean the tutor's arrival time and the time they reach your door are different numbers, and ten minutes of queueing every week pushes the session steadily later. Most societies register a recurring visitor given a name, a phone number and a fixed day and time. Some also want an identity document on file, so ask what is required before the first visit rather than at it.

faqs.question: Is a nearby tutor better than a stronger one further away?
faqs.answer: Only once both are properly qualified for your child's stage and level. Nearness buys reliability and frequency, which matter enormously across a term, but it buys no subject expertise at all. The commonest error on this corridor is hiring the closest available person for a Higher Level subject they last taught three years ago. If the distant tutor is genuinely the right specialist for a scarce subject, take them and accept one weekly session. If the subject is commonly taught, take the near one, because you can be seen twice a week and that is what moves work. Most of the IB home classes in Worli that run for two years began with that choice made deliberately.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Not usually after the first session, and on this corridor that is just as well, since many parents here are working in Lower Parel or BKC past the hour the session starts. For a younger child or a first meeting, having an adult in the flat is sensible. What substitutes for your presence afterwards is the written note: three or four lines each week saying what was covered, what was set and what the tutor is watching. Agree in week one that those notes will arrive, because for a working household they are the entire reporting relationship.

faqs.question: Can we book two sessions a week instead of one long one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most students it is the better structure. Two forty-minute contacts in a week beat one eighty-minute session, because the second contact catches a misunderstanding before a week of practice embeds it. It also suits the attention span of anybody under sixteen far better. The constraint is geography rather than willingness: only a tutor inside the fifteen to twenty-five minute band will agree to two journeys a week at a sensible rate. This is the clearest practical reason to care about distance at all, and it is why we ask for your hour before anything else.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Worli depend on?
faqs.answer: Programme stage, subject scarcity, level, session length and frequency, travel distance, and how much marking happens between sessions. We publish no price list because an honest one does not exist across those variables. A tutor crossing the Sea Link prices an evening differently from one walking from Prabhadevi, and a Higher Level specialist in a rarely taught subject is priced differently from a Mathematics tutor. Ask every tutor to break their rate down along those lines and compare the breakdowns rather than the totals, because the totals hide which of the six factors you are actually paying for.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, better than for most other work. Coursework is written, iterative and document-based, which is exactly what screen sharing suits: the tutor reads a draft, marks it live, and talks through the argument. For an Internal Assessment in a written subject or for Extended Essay supervision, geography is close to irrelevant and you should hire the best reader you can find. Where online struggles is in the moment-to-moment work of a quantitative subject, where a tutor needs to watch a hand write a solution and intervene before the wrong method sets.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them from the same shortlist, usually within a few days, with no lock-in and no notice period. Before switching, it is worth separating two different problems. If the four-week review contains no diagnosis and no evidence, the tutor is the issue and a change is correct. If the diagnosis is clear and specific but your child has done nothing in the six days between sessions, a new face will not help, and the more productive conversation is about what happens when no tutor is in the room.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Ryan Global School, Aditya Birla World Academy, JBCN International School, Parel or any other school named on this page. We mention local schools because their internal assessment calendars determine when tutoring is useful on this corridor and because parents search by school. No tutor on the platform should claim insider knowledge of a school's marking, access to its papers, or any relationship with its staff. Report it if one does and the profile comes down.

faqs.answer: Start with the hour, not the area. Tell us what weekday window genuinely works once school, travel and dinner are accounted for, and we will tell you who can hold it. Then ask your society office about a standing visitor entry, because that is the other thing that decides whether a weekly slot holds.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE programme structure across Mumbai schools
paragraphs: Mumbai runs the full International Baccalaureate (IB) ladder alongside Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel pathways, often inside the same building. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs through middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years, with IGCSE sitting in Years 9 and 10. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE Years 1-12 with a tutor in Mumbai matched per subject rather than per family.

Which rung your child is on should change how far you look. At PYP and early MYP, reliability and patience with a seven-year-old at 4.30pm matter more than subject depth, so genuine proximity wins. A PYP home tutor in Juhu or Malabar Hill should be ten minutes away, because the session is short and lateness eats it. A tutor who is fifteen minutes late to a forty-five minute session has lost a third of it, and a child of that age will not get the lost third back by concentrating harder at the end.

From MYP 4 upward the balance tips. IGCSE splits Mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended tiers, and the tier chosen in Year 9 sets the grade ceiling for a series two years later. At DP the specialism argument wins outright: three Higher Level (HL) and three Standard Level (SL) subjects plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service is a specific combination, and the tutor needs to have taught that level on that board.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessment each subject carries
paragraphs: Every Diploma Programme subject carries an internal assessment (IA), marked by the school and moderated externally, and the IA is where most families discover they need a tutor. Mathematics carries an exploration, the sciences carry a scientific investigation, Language A carries an individual oral, and Visual Arts carries a comparative study alongside an exhibition. Business Management, Economics, History and Psychology each carry a written piece judged against published criteria. None of it is homework, and all of it lands in the same months.

Subject choice across both boards generates the most calls. Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at HL and SL, and a student who took Analysis and Approaches HL because a university application asked for it, without the algebra to carry it, is the most common DP1 rescue request we see in Mumbai. Choosing between Physics HL and Chemistry HL, or dropping a third science for Economics, has the same effect on which tutor you need.

On the Cambridge side the paper and component structure drives the work, from IGCSE Mathematics Extended to the sciences with their practical or alternative-to-practical paper. A tutor who has worked through past papers in that exact component moves faster than one reading the syllabus for the first time alongside your child. This is also why all IB and IGCSE subjects, with a tutor in Mumbai chosen per subject, beats one person stretched across four. A DP2 student might need HL Chemistry weekly and SL Economics only for the six weeks before an IA deadline, and two tutors on two evenings, each on their own route, is steadier than one person covering everything.

sections.heading: Six Mumbai zones, and the routes that actually connect them
paragraphs: South Mumbai is short on distance and long on time. Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Fort, Churchgate, Walkeshwar, Malabar Hill, Tardeo, Worli and Prabhadevi sit within a few kilometres of each other, yet a tutor leaving Worli at 6pm for Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. Tutors here are matched within the island. The Coastal Road has changed the Worli to Marine Lines leg, and Metro Line 3 links Cuffe Parade to BKC, so a tutor teaching in Bandra Kurla Complex in the afternoon can reach a Cuffe Parade family in the evening without touching the Western Express Highway.

The Western Suburbs run north to south and almost nothing runs across them. Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West, Juhu, Vile Parle, Andheri West, Oshiwara, Goregaon East, Malad West, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East are strung along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with Metro Lines 2A and 7 carrying the Dahisar to Andheri leg. Matching along the line works: a Khar West tutor covers Santacruz West and Vile Parle in three stops, and a Malad West tutor covers Kandivali East and Borivali on Metro Line 2A. Matching across it does not. Juhu to Andheri East is six kilometres and two different worlds at 6.30pm.

The Central Suburbs are where distance lies to you most. Kurla, Ghatkopar East, Ghatkopar West, Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg, Powai, Chandivali and Hiranandani Gardens are served by the Central Line, the Eastern Express Highway, JVLR and the SCLR, and Powai has no station of its own. A tutor two kilometres from a Hiranandani Gardens tower but on the far side of Chandivali at 7pm is a forty-minute drive. A tutor in Ghatkopar East reaches Versova in about thirty-five minutes on one Metro Line 1 ride, and Powai in roughly twenty by road up JVLR. On a map the first tutor is nearer. On a Tuesday the second one is the one who arrives.

The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Mankhurd and Wadala up to Bhandup and Mulund West, gain more from the Eastern Freeway than anywhere else in the city. A Chembur tutor reaches Cuffe Parade faster in the evening peak than a Worli tutor does, which is the clearest illustration of why a nearest-first list is the wrong instrument. The Harbour Line and the Monorail between Chembur and Wadala fill in the short hops.

Navi Mumbai is built in nodes, so its routes are unusually clean. Vashi, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar, Airoli, Ulwe and Panvel sit along the Harbour Line, Palm Beach Road and the Sion to Panvel Highway, with Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 running Belapur to Pendhar and the Trans-Harbour Line linking Thane to Vashi. A Nerul tutor covering Vashi and Belapur on Palm Beach Road is a twenty-minute hop each way. The Atal Setu has made Ulwe and Panvel to Sewri quick, though a tutor pulled across the creek from the island city for a 6pm weekday lesson rarely lasts a full term.

Thane is set by one road. Thane West, Vartak Nagar, Majiwada, Pokhran Road, Manpada, Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali spread west to east along Ghodbunder Road, with the Central Line and the Trans-Harbour Line at the station end. A tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes at noon and closer to an hour at 7.30pm: the same tutor and the same distance giving two different answers. Thane tutors are matched within Thane, and Mulund tutors crossing the Eastern Express Highway are the one regular exception. So when you search for an IB tutor near me in Mumbai, we read your address as a point on a corridor rather than the centre of a circle. Mumbai, Maharashtra is a city of lines, and the lines decide whether 6pm on Tuesday still holds in March.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school calendar does to tutor availability
paragraphs: Most IB schools in Mumbai run an August to May year for the May examination session, which gives nearly every family in the city the same four pressure points. Late October stacks MYP and DP internal deadlines against the run-in to mock examinations. January is heaviest: the TOK essay, several IA drafts and mocks inside a few weeks. February and March carry final IA submissions, April is study leave and May is the examinations themselves.

Cambridge IGCSE families sit on a slightly different clock, with mocks in December and January, the main series in May and June, and resits in the October and November series. The two calendars collide in a household with a DP2 student and an IGCSE sibling, because both want the same evening slots in the same eight weeks.

Families we work with attend schools across the city: Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Their calendars set the pressure points, not ours. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools, or with the IB or Cambridge boards.

The calendar is also why the near-me instinct fails hardest in January. Good tutors fill their January weeks in October, so a search started during mock season finds the two-kilometre pool already booked, and the tutor who still has a Tuesday free is on a corridor you had not considered.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one survives a Mumbai commute?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead service and the default, and it works well when your address sits on a route a tutor already travels. Online works when the subject is scarce or the journey is long. Hybrid, meaning one home session and one online session a week, is where most DP families in Mumbai end up by term two.

A home tutor in Mumbai gives you things a screen cannot: written work on paper, which matters in Mathematics and the sciences where method marks live in the working; a student who cannot quietly open another tab; a parent who can hear the session from the next room. For PYP and MYP students, and for anyone starting at 4pm straight after school, we would keep all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai rather than move any of it to a screen.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves the two problems geography creates. One is scarcity: a Higher Level subject with few teachers in the city may have nobody at all on your corridor. The other is the commute, because a tutor spending ninety minutes travelling for a sixty-minute session starts cancelling by week six, whatever they promised in week one. The honest cost of online is engagement, and you usually know within three sessions which kind of student you have.

Hybrid is the arrangement that holds. One home session for written work and the relationship, one online for drill and IA feedback where screen sharing beats paper. It also survives the monsoon. If you came here searching for IB home tuition near me in Mumbai and the right specialist is three zones away, hybrid is how you get them without pretending the drive is sustainable.

sections.heading: How is an IB home tutor in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is checked on identity, on the board and level they claim to teach, and on their stated subject experience before a profile reaches a family. We confirm they have taught the specific programme, IB or IGCSE, at the level they are offering. We do not verify outcomes, and we will not pretend otherwise.

What we check: government identity, qualification claims, which board and which levels, and which subjects and components they have actually taught. A tutor offering HL Chemistry is asked about the internal assessment and the paper structure. One offering IGCSE Mathematics is asked whether they have taught Extended. References from previous families are requested where they exist.

What you should check yourself takes four minutes on the first call. Ask which syllabus version and session they last taught. Ask how they would approach an IA draft that has data but no analysis. Then ask the question that predicts reliability better than any other: where are your other Tuesday families? A tutor who answers Khar West and Santacruz West, when you live in Khar West, has a route. A tutor whose other families are in Mulund and Panvel, and who has agreed to a Bandra West slot, is telling you about week six whether they mean to or not.

Ask the practical things before the first session too: whether they carry past papers or expect you to print them, whether they are comfortable with your society's visitor protocol, and whether they can hold the same slot through January. An IB tutor near me in Mumbai who clears all four of those is a better bet than a closer one who clears two.

sections.heading: Why is the nearest IB tutor rarely the right IB tutor?
paragraphs: Because distance and travel time barely correlate in this city. A nearest-first list sorts tutors by a number that does not predict whether they will arrive. The number that does predict it is whether your address sits on a corridor the tutor already travels on that weekday. Distance is a proxy for that, and a weak one.

Take three tutors and one family in Powai. Tutor A lives two kilometres away in Chandivali but teaches in Andheri West on Tuesdays, so Tuesday evening means crossing the Western Express Highway twice. Tutor B lives in Ghatkopar East, nine kilometres away, and already teaches in Hiranandani Gardens on Tuesdays, reaching you up JVLR in twenty minutes. Tutor C lives in Vikhroli, six kilometres away, with no Tuesday in this direction at all. A nearest-first list ranks them A, C, B. The right order is B, then nobody. There is no single best IB tutor in Mumbai for a slot, only the tutor whose Tuesday already passes your gate.

Thinking in corridors instead of circles is a two-minute exercise. Find your line and your road. In Santacruz West your corridor is the Western Line and Link Road, running from Bandra West up to Borivali, and a tutor anywhere along it is plausible. In Chembur your corridors are the Harbour Line, the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway, which puts Wadala, Mulund West and, in the evening, Cuffe Parade within reach. In Thane West it is Ghodbunder Road and the Central Line, and the only real question is which end of Ghodbunder Road. In Nerul, Palm Beach Road and the Harbour Line give you Vashi, Seawoods and Belapur, and the Atal Setu gives you Sewri.

The one question to ask is where the tutor's other families on that weekday live. It does three jobs at once. It tells you whether your slot is an addition to a trip they were making anyway or a brand new trip, and additions survive. It tells you whether the tutor is being realistic about their own week. And it tells you whether they have taught in your kind of building and school before.

Proximity does genuinely matter in four situations, and there the near-me instinct is right. Young children: a PYP or MYP 1 student at 4.30pm needs a tutor ten minutes away, because the session is short and lateness eats it. Early starts: anything beginning at or before 4.30pm has to come from someone who is not crossing the city to get there. Heavy materials: a DP Visual Arts or Design Technology session with work to carry, or a tutor bringing past paper bundles. Back-to-back siblings: two sessions in one visit only works if the tutor arrives fresh rather than an hour into their evening.

There is also the opposite case, where you should widen on purpose. If your child takes a Higher Level subject that few schools in Mumbai offer, the pool is small and unevenly spread across the city, so insisting on a two-kilometre radius for HL Further Mathematics, HL Music or a less common Group 2 language at HL returns either nobody or somebody who has not taught it. Widen to the corridor, then the zone, then online, in that order. Searching for IB tutors near me Mumbai is the right instinct for SL Business Management and the wrong one for a scarce HL.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process rather than marks. The student brings the right materials unprompted, knows what the next assessment is, and can say what went wrong on the last one. Homework arguments drop. If none of that has shifted after four sessions, the match is wrong, and that is a matching problem to raise rather than a student problem to accept.

At one term the gains show in internal assessment drafts and class tests before they show in a predicted grade. A Physics IA that had a method and no uncertainty analysis in October has both by December. A Mathematics exploration has a question narrow enough to answer. An IGCSE student who was guessing on structured questions starts showing working that earns method marks.

At one exam cycle, the May session for most Mumbai schools, the honest position is simple: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anyone who does is selling you something. A good tutor changes preparation, timing and the quality of coursework submitted. They do not change how much the student does in the hours between sessions. Hold us to the parts we control: the right tutor, on time, on the right syllabus, with work marked between visits.

If it is not working, say so in week three rather than week ten, and name the specific problem, because the fix differs. A pace mismatch is usually solved by changing the plan; a style mismatch needs a different tutor, and a replacement is arranged without you restarting the search. On cost, IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on board, level, subject scarcity, travel and session length. An IB private tutor Mumbai families book for one HL subject is priced differently from a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents want covered in a single weekly visit.

sections.heading: Starting home classes with an IB tutor near me in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have four things ready: the board and year group, the subjects and levels, your address down to the building and tower, and the two or three weekly windows you can actually hold. The fourth is the one families guess at, and guessing there is what produces a match that fails in week five.

Also useful, though not required: the last report card or a recent marked assessment, the next two deadlines from the school calendar, and one sentence on what the student finds hardest. A tutor who reads a marked IA draft beforehand arrives with a plan instead of spending the first hour diagnosing.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to work through a past paper or a draft, find the two or three specific gaps, and finish by saying what the next four sessions will cover and what should be done between them. If they leave without saying that, ask. IB home tuition in Mumbai is worth watching closely in week one, because that is when it is cheap to change.

Set-up matters more than it sounds. A table, not a bed. A room where the door can be closed but is not locked. Someone at home for the first few sessions at least. And the tutor's name left at the gate for a standing weekly slot, so nobody loses ten minutes in the lobby every week. If the session runs at 7.30pm, check that the lift and the lobby lighting are not under maintenance on that weekday, because in older buildings in Mumbai that is a real reason sessions start late.

faqs.question: Do you actually have a tutor near me, or will someone travel an hour to get here?
faqs.answer: Both happen, and we tell you which one you are getting. For most addresses in the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs and Navi Mumbai there is a tutor already working on your corridor, and the journey is twenty to thirty minutes. For a scarce Higher Level subject, or an unusual slot, the honest answer may be that the only qualified tutor is forty minutes away. Where the journey is genuinely long, we will propose a hybrid pattern instead of pretending the drive is sustainable through a Mumbai monsoon.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my address is on a tutor's route?
faqs.answer: Ask where their other families on that weekday live, and whether they are travelling from home or from another session. Those two answers tell you almost everything. A tutor coming to Khar West from a Santacruz West session is adding fifteen minutes to a trip they were making anyway. A tutor coming to Khar West from Mulund on the same evening is making a new trip, and new trips are the ones that get rescheduled in July. The profile we send names the corridor the tutor already works, so you can check this before the call.

faqs.question: Is online better than a long drive?
faqs.answer: For a sixty-minute weekly session, yes, once the drive passes about forty-five minutes each way. A tutor who spends ninety minutes travelling will start rescheduling, and rescheduling damages a term more than a screen does. The exception is a young student, or any session before 4.30pm, where a short home visit beats a better online tutor. If you searched for IB tuition near me in Mumbai and the right subject specialist is three zones away, the stable arrangement is usually one home session a week plus one online, rather than two long drives.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road for a 7pm slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the tutor should be based on the eastern half of Ghodbunder Road, not near Thane station. The same journey takes twenty minutes at noon and close to an hour at 7.30pm, so the starting point decides whether 7pm is realistic at all. We match within Thane for exactly this reason: Thane West, Vartak Nagar, Majiwada, Manpada, Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali are one corridor with very different evening timings along it. A Mulund tutor crossing the Eastern Express Highway can work for a weekend slot and usually not for a weekday evening one.

faqs.question: Our society needs a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work for a weekly session?
faqs.answer: Leave a standing entry for the tutor at the gate before the first session and the problem disappears. Most societies here will register a recurring visitor for a fixed day and time once a resident confirms it, either in the visitor app or at the security desk. Without it the tutor loses five to ten minutes in the lobby every week, which adds up to most of a session across a term, paid for and spent on a clipboard. Tell us if your building needs the tutor's identity details in advance and we will send them with the profile.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition?
faqs.answer: For the first two or three sessions, yes, at least somewhere in the house. After that it depends on the age of the student. For PYP and MYP students we would keep an adult at home throughout. For DP students many families stop sitting in by the second month, though keeping the session in a shared room rather than a bedroom is worth maintaining. What matters more than supervision is the set-up: a table, a door that closes but does not lock, and a phone that lives in another room for the hour.

faqs.question: What if the only tutor for my HL subject is in another zone?
faqs.answer: Widen in a specific order: the whole corridor, then the whole zone, then online. For a Higher Level subject that few schools in the city offer, the pool is small and not spread evenly, so a two-kilometre radius returns either nobody or somebody who has not taught that level. A tutor in Ghatkopar East who has taught HL Chemistry to the current syllabus is more useful to a Powai student than a Chandivali generalist, and Metro Line 1 plus JVLR make that match work in practice rather than only on paper.

faqs.question: Do you cover IGCSE as well as IB, and can one tutor do both?
faqs.answer: Yes to coverage, and sometimes to one tutor, depending on the subjects. A Mathematics tutor who teaches both IGCSE Extended and DP Analysis and Approaches is common, and useful in a household with an IGCSE sibling and a DP student. Across the sciences and humanities the boards diverge enough in assessment that we usually match separately, because DP internal assessment criteria and IGCSE paper and practical structure reward different preparation. If you want one tutor for a sibling pair, say so at the start and we will filter for it.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel and session length, in roughly that order. A Higher Level subject with few teachers available costs more than a Standard Level one with many. A tutor crossing a zone prices the travel in, which is one more reason corridor matching tends to save money. Longer sessions usually cost less per hour than short ones, and a fixed weekly slot held for a term is treated differently from occasional sessions before a deadline. We do not publish a price list, because any single number would be wrong for most families.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us the specific problem and we arrange a replacement without you restarting the search. We ask what exactly is wrong, because the fix differs. If the pace is off, the tutor can change the plan and often should. If the student has stopped talking in sessions, that is a style mismatch and a different tutor is the answer. The replacement is briefed on what has been covered so the new tutor does not start from zero, and we would much rather hear this in week three than at the end of a term.

faqs.question: What happens to a session if the roads flood or the train is delayed?
faqs.answer: It moves online for that evening rather than being lost. Between June and September, Mumbai hands everyone a few unusable evenings, and the families who come through the monsoon with their schedule intact are the ones who agreed a fallback in advance. We ask every tutor to keep an online option ready for exactly this. If the tutor cannot teach at all that day, the session is rescheduled, usually to the weekend, and a slot missed in January is worth chasing rather than writing off.

sections.heading: How IB Gram turns a diagnosis into a tutor shortlist in Mumbai
paragraphs: Most enquiries arrive as one sentence: my daughter is in DP1 at a school in Bandra West and her Chemistry has gone from a 6 to a 4. That sentence is a symptom, not a diagnosis. The first thing we ask for is the last marked paper, or the last report with the subject teacher's comments on it, because what the marker wrote in the margin tells us far more than the grade does. A script with short, unfinished answers and whole questions left blank is a content problem. A script where the chemistry is right, the working is right, and the marks still go missing is a technique problem. Those two need different tutors, and sending the wrong one costs a term.

The order of the process matters more than its speed. 1. You send the year, the board, the subject and the one thing that changed, with the marked paper if you have it. 2. We read the paper and tell you which of the five common problems it looks like, including the cases where the answer is not a tutor. 3. We shortlist people who have taught that subject at that level, filtered first by whether they can actually reach your building on the evening you want. 4. You speak to one or two of them yourself before anything is booked. 5. The first session is a diagnostic hour that ends with the tutor writing down what they found, in enough detail that you could hand the note to the school.

Travel is a filter, not an afterthought. A tutor living in Juhu can promise a seven o'clock Tuesday slot in Chembur and mean it in week one; by week six the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road has quietly ended that arrangement, and the family is the one apologising. We match inside a corridor wherever the subject allows it, and we say plainly when a scarce subject such as Further Mathematics, Design Technology or a second language means a longer journey, a weekend slot or online sessions instead.

We also turn requests down, which is the part of this that no advertisement describes. If a parent describes a child who has stopped opening books at all, or a student who is in the wrong board rather than behind in it, a weekly tutor is not the first move. Saying that loses us the booking and saves the family four months, and it is the only version of this service worth running.

sections.heading: Which programme is the problem actually sitting in: IGCSE, MYP or DP?
paragraphs: Work backwards from the assessment the student is sitting this year. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) a falling grade is usually a criterion problem. In International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Years 10 and 11 it is more often a content gap, because those papers reward recall and clean method. In the Diploma Programme (DP) it is most often workload. The same two-grade drop therefore means three different things.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the MYP and the DP, and many Mumbai schools pair an IGCSE pathway in Years 9 to 11 with the IB DP in Years 11 and 12, so one child can live through two boards in five years. MYP sciences are marked against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student who can recite the content and cannot plan a fair test scores just as badly as one who knows nothing, and only the criterion breakdown shows which it is. In PYP and the lower MYP years, what gets described as weakness in a subject is frequently reading stamina, and a subject tutor will spend a term treating the wrong thing.

The Core and Extended decision in IGCSE Mathematics, the sciences and some languages produces more avoidable tutoring than any other single choice. A student placed on Extended because the family wanted the higher ceiling, who then loses marks on every multi-step question, has a placement problem that a tutor can only partly carry. A student sitting Core who needs Extended to take a DP Higher Level subject has a genuine content gap with a fixed deadline attached, and that one is exactly what tutoring is for. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both publish the tier descriptions; the school's subject teacher can tell you in one email which tier the student is actually on.

At DP the Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) fork does the same job. HL adds topics, longer papers and more depth, and the honest test of whether an HL subject is wrong is not the grade but how many hours a week it eats out of the other five. Add the DP core, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service, and you have the workload diagnosis rather than the knowledge one.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: marks lost on knowledge, marks lost on the presentation of knowledge
paragraphs: Mathematics is where the two gaps separate most cleanly. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, a content gap shows as a blank page or an abandoned part (b). A technique gap shows as a correct final answer with no method lines, a correct method with no units, an exact answer where the paper asked for three significant figures, or a graphical question solved by hand when the paper expected the calculator. The second student is often stronger at mathematics than the first and scores lower, which is why the grade alone sends families to the wrong tutor.

The DP sciences put the same split inside one piece of coursework. A Physics, Chemistry or Biology Internal Assessment (IA) is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and the marks most commonly lost are in evaluation, where students list limitations instead of explaining what each limitation did to the result. No amount of extra physics content fixes that; it is a writing and reasoning job, and it is learnable in a handful of sessions. IGCSE science papers lose marks somewhere else entirely, usually on command words: a question that says state does not want a paragraph, and a question that says explain does not accept a label.

Humanities and languages are almost entirely presentation. A History Paper 2 answer that narrates two case studies without comparing them has the knowledge and not the structure. An Economics commentary without a correctly labelled diagram and a real-world link has done the economics and left the marks on the table. English Language and Literature Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text, and the standard failure is quotation without comment: the evidence is on the page and nobody said what it does. If your child can talk fluently about the novel and writes fours, you are looking at technique.

Subject choice across both boards is part of the diagnosis rather than a separate conversation. Few families need all IB and IGCSE subjects from one tutor in Mumbai; most need one subject diagnosed properly, one internal assessment unblocked, and the rest left alone. Each subject carries its own coursework with its own internal school deadline, so a second tutor added in November is usually a workload decision disguised as an academic one.

sections.heading: Finding an IB home tutor in Mumbai: what each of the six zones means for a weekday slot
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is not one tutoring market but six, and the zone decides which diagnoses you can realistically treat on a weekday evening. South Mumbai is short distances and slow movement: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo and Fort sit minutes apart on a map and forty minutes apart at seven in the evening, so tutors here are matched inside the island rather than brought down the Western Line from the suburbs. The Coastal Road and the Bandra–Worli Sea Link changed the Worli to Bandra West run far more than they changed anything between Haji Ali and Churchgate, and Metro Line 3 has started to make a BKC tutor viable in Cuffe Parade.

The Western Suburbs run north and south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, which means matching along the line works and matching across it does not. Bandra West to Khar West to Santacruz West is one market; Juhu and Andheri West is another; Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar form a third, now stitched together by Metro Lines 2A and 7 and by Link Road for anyone willing to drive. The practical meaning of searching for an IB home tutor in Mumbai is therefore a question about your corridor before it is a question about the tutor.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Ghatkopar or Kanjurmarg, and a monsoon evening on JVLR can take a session off the calendar. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Fort closer to Chembur and Wadala than the map suggests, which occasionally makes a South Mumbai specialist workable for a weekend slot.

Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short drives apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and the Belapur to Pendhar metro in support. The Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing, but pulling a tutor over it for a weekday evening lesson rarely holds for a full term. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the timetable more than any tutor's preference does.

sections.heading: When each problem surfaces in the Mumbai IB school year
paragraphs: The calendar is predictable enough to plan around. Most Mumbai international schools open the academic year in the first half of the calendar year, the DP cohort works towards the May examination session, and IGCSE candidates sit either the May and June or the October and November series. Content gaps surface in the first set of unit tests, within about six weeks of a new year starting. Technique gaps hide all year and appear in mock examinations, because classwork is forgiving and a mark scheme is not. The IA, EE and TOK collision lands in the stretch of months before mocks, when three pieces of coursework have school deadlines set earlier than the board's.

Disengagement has its own season. It shows up after a long break, most often the Diwali weeks or the gap after mocks, when a student who was coping on momentum stops and nobody can tell whether it is tiredness, something social, or a subject they have privately given up on. School-fit problems appear in the first term after a change: a new school, a new board, or a move from IGCSE into the DP where the same student is suddenly asked to write rather than to recall. If you know which month you are in, you already have a shortlist of two or three likely diagnoses.

Families we work with attend schools including Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Chembur and Parel, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Each sets internal deadlines inside the board's external ones, which is why two DP2 students in the same tower can have entirely different pressure weeks. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools or with any examination board.

Before hiring anyone, send the subject teacher two questions by email: which criterion or question type is costing the marks, and is the student's level or tier placement right. Teachers answer this more often than parents expect, and the reply frequently removes the need for a tutor or changes which tutor you need. It also gives the tutor a starting point that is not guesswork.
