faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our building in Cuffe Parade, and how does gate access work?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tuition is the lead service and the tutor travels to you. Maker Towers and Jolly Maker Apartments both keep visitor records at the gate, as do most societies along the seafront, so the practical step is lodging the tutor's name and number with your society office once at the start of the term. After that weekly entry is routine. We confirm each tutor's actual travel origin before sending the profile, because a stated willingness to travel and a sustainable commute are different things.

faqs.question: What do I have to pay before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The brief, the shortlist and the discovery calls are all free, and lessons begin only after you have chosen a tutor and said yes. Fees are agreed between you and the tutor on the discovery call, which is where you should get a specific figure rather than a range. There is no package to buy, no minimum number of sessions and no notice period, so the arrangement continues because the reviews are positive rather than because you are committed to it.

faqs.question: What is in the review every two to four weeks?
faqs.answer: A short written note covering what was taught, what was set, what came back, and what the tutor currently thinks the core problem is. We ask for it in writing because written reviews are harder to be vague in than phone calls. If a review says progress is good without naming anything specific, we press on it before you have to. Families here commonly use the review to reshape the arrangement rather than the tutor, moving the slot earlier or shifting a session online during the monsoon.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find a tutor for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the week. Mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and economics usually produce a shortlist quickly even at Higher Level, because the local pool is deepest in those. Design technology, visual arts, music and uncommon languages may not be fillable inside the island at all on a specific weekday evening, and the honest answer there is an excellent online specialist rather than an approximately qualified local tutor. Requests made during the neighbourhood's coursework deadline fortnight take longer whatever the subject.

faqs.question: Can we switch tutors without paying a penalty?
faqs.answer: Yes, at any point, with no notice period and no fee. Tell us what specifically is not working and we match again, because precision improves the replacement: too slow, too abstract, sets no work, and talks to the parent instead of the child point at four different people. We ask the departing tutor for a short handover so the new one does not restart from the beginning. Mismatches are more common than families expect and usually reflect temperament rather than competence.

faqs.question: Do you work with students from B.D. Somani International School?
faqs.answer: We work with families living in this neighbourhood, many of whose children attend it, and we have no relationship with the school itself. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with B.D. Somani International School, Cathedral and John Connon School, or any institution. What is genuinely useful is that a tutor already teaching several families in Cuffe Parade knows which part of a current assessment is causing trouble before school feedback arrives. Tutors have no access to school systems and see no internal marks unless you share them.

faqs.question: Which nearby areas do you cover with the same tutors?
faqs.answer: Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Nariman Point and Fort, which function as one scheduling unit because a single tutor can run evening lessons across all four without the commute degrading. Churchgate is the station most tutors arrive at and the Harbour Line serves the Colaba end, while Metro Line 3 has brought the Bandra Kurla Complex side into range for scarcer subjects. Further north the arithmetic fails for a weekday evening, and we will tell you that rather than place a tutor whose availability will quietly erode.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle more than one subject for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and we will tell you when the request is not credible. In the middle years one tutor across several subject groups often works. At Diploma level, genuine depth in three Higher Level subjects is uncommon, and a tutor stretched across them tends to drift into general study support. If that is the shape of your brief we come back with a question rather than a shortlist. One strong subject specialist usually produces more change than a generalist covering everything at a shallower depth.

faqs.question: Do you offer online tuition if the evening travel does not work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some situations it is the better choice rather than the compromise. Online is right when the specialism is scarce enough that geography would force a worse match, when a student needs a short clarification that does not justify anyone's travel, and when monsoon evenings make a fixed slot in this part of the city unreliable. Most families here end up hybrid: one anchored weekly session at home plus a short online slot when something has gone wrong mid-week.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, not introduction. The tutor should give your child something slightly beyond their current level and watch where they stop, because the stall point is the useful information. Expect relatively little explaining in that first hour, and expect a specific sentence at the end about what the tutor believes the actual problem is: proportional reasoning, command-term handling, a missing foundation, or something non-academic. Judge the tutor on how specific that sentence is. More practice is a description, not a diagnosis, and you should ask for better.

faqs.question: Why should I use a platform instead of asking for a recommendation?
faqs.answer: Recommendations work well and we would not argue against a good one. What a platform adds is verification you cannot easily do yourself, identity, qualification by subject and board experience checked before you spend an evening on a call, plus a replacement route that does not involve an awkward conversation with the neighbour who recommended them. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families find by word of mouth may be excellent; the risk is that leaving is socially expensive, and that changes how long a poor match survives.

sections.heading: Sending IB Gram a brief from Cumballa Hill
paragraphs: A brief is four lines and takes two minutes, and the quality of it determines almost everything that follows. Line one: year and programme. Line two: subject and level or tier. Line three: school. Line four: what is going wrong, in your words. That fourth line is where the matching actually happens, because a sentence like cannot start an unfamiliar question points at a specific habit, while needs help with Maths points at nobody in particular.

What happens next runs in a fixed order. 1. We read the brief and come back with one or two questions, almost always about level and about which evenings are genuinely free. 2. We shortlist two or three verified tutors who have taught that board at that level recently and who already work inside the island city. 3. You get the profiles, each with a reason and an honest caveat. 4. You take a free discovery call with whoever you prefer. 5. Lessons start only once you have said yes to a named person.

Households on this hill often send two briefs rather than one, and we would rather they did. Cumballa Hill feeds Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo, which runs both the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) and Cambridge IGCSE, so one flat can hold a Diploma second year and a Year 10 on the Cambridge route. Those get matched separately. Bundling them into one request to save effort is how a family ends up with a tutor who is right for one child and adequate for the other. IB Gram home tuition in Cumballa Hill is arranged per child for exactly that reason.

The part that is slower than parents want is a scarce subject. A thinly taught Higher Level (HL) combination or a less commonly taught language can take several days to shortlist properly, and we take them. An IB Gram home tutor in Cumballa Hill who has not actually taught the level is worse than waiting, because the cost of unwinding a wrong match in October is a term rather than a week.

sections.heading: Which programmes and tiers we cover in Cumballa Hill
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate across the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme, plus Cambridge International Education at IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel where a school follows it. On the Diploma side that means Higher Level and Standard Level (SL), with the Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject and the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) alongside. On the Cambridge side it means the Core and Extended tier decision and the papers that follow from it.

We press on level and tier before sending anyone, because this is where mismatches are born. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters: the same content returns with a longer chain of reasoning expected, and an answer that scored at Standard Level begins losing marks. A tutor who has only taught to Standard Level will teach well and still leave a Higher Level student short, and nobody notices until the first mock. On the Cambridge route, whether your child is entered for Core or Extended changes what should be taught at all.

Internal assessment support is available across subjects with a boundary we do not move. A tutor can narrow a research question until it is answerable in the available weeks, teach how evidence is handled, and read a draft and say where a conclusion overreaches. A tutor cannot write any part of it, and should refuse if asked. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Cumballa Hill is asked for, that line is identical, and a candidate who negotiates on it is telling you how the term will go.

What we will not do is claim coverage we do not have this week. If no verified tutor is free for your subject and level in the window you need, we say so plainly rather than offering an adjacent specialism and hoping. Your school's coordinator and the current subject guide remain the authority on how your child's course is structured, since the boards revise them on their own cycles and we would rather you trusted the source.

sections.heading: What should a subject brief say to be useful?
paragraphs: It should name the symptom rather than the subject. Mathematics is not a brief; a student who can follow a worked example and freezes on an unfamiliar question is a brief, and it points at algebraic fluency and confidence. A Higher Level student who understands everything and finishes nothing in the time allowed is a different brief entirely and needs a different tutor, because that is a pace and technique problem rather than a knowledge one.

The same holds across subjects, and the patterns are consistent enough to be useful. In the sciences, marks usually go missing on explanation and on investigation design rather than on content: a student restates a trend instead of giving its cause, or chooses a research question nobody could answer in the weeks available. In English, the diagnosis is almost always that a capable writer summarises where the criteria ask for analysis. In the humanities, it is opinion offered where sourced evidence was required. In languages, it is production rather than comprehension.

If you can name which of those your child is doing, the shortlist gets sharper and the first session gets faster. If you cannot, send the marked work instead and let the tutor do it, which is a legitimate use of the discovery call. What does not help is the report's own phrasing, because school comments are written to be diplomatic and a tutor reading lacks depth has learned very little. A good brief is the cheapest part of arranging home tuition and the part that decides most of it.

For families needing several subjects covered, we would rather arrange two tutors on lighter schedules than stretch one person across four. Related pairs genuinely work, Mathematics with Physics, English with History, and we suggest them where they fit. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents sometimes hope to find does not exist, and a candidate claiming to be one has answered the question before you asked it.

sections.heading: Why does IB Gram match tutors inside the island?
paragraphs: Because a slot that cannot be reached reliably is not a slot, and in South Mumbai that has nothing to do with distance. A tutor crossing from Worli or Dadar covers a handful of kilometres and can still lose the evening at the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals, with the Kemps Corner flyover adding its own delay in the peak. A tutor already teaching in Kemps Corner, Breach Candy or Tardeo reaches a flat on Cumballa Hill in minutes and can run two lessons in one evening without using a main road.

That is why we filter for the island before we filter for anything else except subject and level. It is also why we sometimes decline a match a parent asks for. If you want a particular tutor who lives in Kandivali for a 5pm Tuesday, we will tell you it will not survive November rather than take the booking and watch it decay into fortnightly sessions nobody formally agreed to. Searches for IB tutors near me in Cumballa Hill are pointing at precisely the right instinct.

Grant Road is the nearest station and the usual arrival route for a commuting tutor, with a short rickshaw from there. The Coastal Road has made the approach from Worli more predictable in the evening and Metro Line 3 has changed access from Cuffe Parade and Fort. Neither changes the last stretch, which is why a tutor arriving by train is frequently in the flat before one who left Bandra by car at the same time.

The exception is scarcity and it is real. For a thinly taught Higher Level subject the right verified specialist may be in the Western Suburbs, Thane or outside Mumbai altogether, and then we propose weekly online lessons rather than a commute nobody will sustain past the second month. Some families already have an IB private tutor Cumballa Hill neighbours recommended and come to us for the other child, which is a sensible way to use a platform rather than a failure of one.

sections.heading: Term dates, reports and the Mumbai weeks that matter
paragraphs: Scheduling here is set by the school year rather than by us, and the schools on this hill are few enough to name. Families attend Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo, which runs both the Diploma Programme and IGCSE, Activity High School on Peddar Road, and Bombay International School at Babulnath. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Aditya Birla World Academy, Activity High School, Bombay International School or any other school named on this page. Their term dates and reporting cycles are simply what determines when tutors have capacity.

The year opens in June and the gentle first weeks are when a Diploma first year slips without anybody noticing. The monsoon term brings the first internal assessments and the first candid report, which is what sends most families looking. October and November bring mid-terms. January and February are the heaviest weeks for a Diploma second year, with mocks, internal assessments in final form, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge arriving together, while an IGCSE student's pinch point is the tier decision and then the spring papers.

For a two-board household the overlap is the thing to plan for. Both children's heaviest weeks land in the same stretch without matching exactly, and one shared evening slot will be contested in February. We ask families to map both calendars in August and decide in advance whose session has priority in a clash, which sounds bureaucratic and removes a genuinely unpleasant argument later.

Two further realities. Heavy rain costs Mumbai, Maharashtra schools days, and a lost school day usually costs the tuition evening too because the tutor is in the same weather, so the make-up rule should exist in writing before July. And examination leave empties the calendar suddenly in spring, which is the natural window for a short intensive block rather than a weekly hour.

sections.heading: Home tuition first in Mumbai, with online used on purpose
paragraphs: The default arrangement is a tutor in the flat, and we will argue for it unless there is a specific reason otherwise. A tutor in the room sees the working, the hesitation and the wrong line while it is being written, and stops a bad method before it has been practised for half an hour. That is where most of the value sits in the earlier stages of any course, which is why IB Gram home tuition in Cumballa Hill leads with lessons in the apartment rather than video calls with travel as an afterthought.

Online is the right answer in three identifiable cases. A scarce specialist outside reach, where the correct person on a screen beats a nearby approximation. Short, frequent work in the final months, where twenty minutes on one marked script outperforms a long lesson. And a late slot after a school commitment, since an IB online tutor in Cumballa Hill can take nine o'clock and a travelling tutor cannot. We propose it in those cases rather than treating it as a fallback.

Hybrid is where most families here settle, and for a two-child household it is often the only sane shape. One child in the room on a weekday evening, the other online on a different day, which keeps the table free, spreads the week and halves the travel being priced in. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Cumballa Hill drift towards some version of this by the second term whether or not anybody planned it.

Changing mode mid-term is normal and does not need renegotiating from scratch: tell the tutor, agree the new rhythm, keep the review date. What we discourage is drifting into online because one week was difficult, since an in-person habit that lapses for a fortnight rarely returns. If travel genuinely is not working, change the arrangement deliberately at a review rather than letting it erode week by week.

sections.heading: What a verified profile from us means, and what it does not
paragraphs: It means four things have been confirmed: who the person is, what they hold, which subjects and levels they claim, and whether they have recently taught the board in question. The fourth carries most of the weight, because subject knowledge is rarely the gap. A strong degree with no exposure to the Diploma Programme produces a tutor who teaches the subject well and the course badly, missing the command terms, the internal assessment criteria and the way marks are actually awarded. So we ask for levels and recent years, and we ask a candidate to explain how they would move one specific weak student forward.

It does not mean the tutor is right for your child. No screening can establish that, and a platform implying its badge settles the matter is overselling what a check can do. The free discovery call is the instrument, and it works best treated as an interview rather than a courtesy: bring the last report and one piece of marked work, hand it over, and listen to how the tutor reacts to it.

The checks that are yours rather than ours are short and worth running. Ask what arrives in writing at four weeks. Ask what the tutor expects your child to do between sessions, because a tutor with no answer plans to explain rather than to teach. Ask what they would refuse to do. And be wary of anybody offering a guaranteed grade or quoting a success rate: boards set grade boundaries each session, no honest tutor promises a number, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades.

There is one check that belongs to buildings rather than to people. Lessons here happen inside the flat, so a tutor holding a recurring weekly slot needs clearing with your building's visitor procedure before the first visit rather than at the lobby desk on the night. We confirm how your building handles a repeat visitor and whether anything is needed from you each time, and the tutor is briefed on it in advance, as every home tutor working these buildings should be. An uncleared tutor loses a real slice of a one-hour lesson, and an unplanned extra session before a mock becomes much harder to arrange.

sections.heading: How does the review cycle work once home tuition starts?
paragraphs: Every two to four weeks you get one page, and the date is fixed before the first lesson rather than arranged afterwards. The page names what was diagnosed, what has changed, what has not, and what the next block targets. It is deliberately short, because a long report is easy to write and hard to act on, and a page a parent actually reads is worth more than three a parent files. Every IB Gram home tutor in Cumballa Hill writes it, including the ones who would rather talk.

The first review is the important one, and what it should not contain is a grade. Four weeks is long enough to diagnose and begin correcting and nowhere near long enough to move an examination mark. So the first page is mostly diagnosis: the two or three specific things your child was doing that cost marks, which has already shifted, and what the tutor intends next. If the page instead says sessions are going well, ask once for specifics and treat a second vague answer as a decision.

The review is also the natural place to change something. Add a second subject, move to hybrid, shorten the sessions and make them more frequent, pause for examination leave, or stop. We would far rather a family stopped at a review point than drifted into a term of quiet resentment, which is what happens when there is no scheduled moment to say this is not working.

Replacement runs on the same logic and carries no penalty, no notice period and no minimum term. Tell us what specifically is wrong, whether that is timekeeping, no work being set, explanations the child cannot follow, or simply two people who do not get on, and each of those points at a different second profile. Vague unhappiness is still worth sending; precision gets you a better replacement faster. For a household running two children, we keep one review conversation covering both so you are not having the same discussion twice.

sections.heading: Where we say no, and what we never claim
paragraphs: We do not guarantee grades. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will, because boards set grade boundaries each session and the person sitting the paper is a teenager rather than a process. We publish no success rate, no student count and no average improvement, for the plain reason that we could not verify any figure we printed, and an unverifiable number on a tutoring page is marketing wearing the clothes of evidence.

We also decline work. If the subject choice was wrong and the school still allows a change, change the subject rather than buying two years of support for a decision nobody believes in. If no work is happening between sessions, the first problem is structure at home and a tutor becomes an expensive supervisor. If a child is not attending lessons at school, that conversation comes before this one. And if four subjects are failing simultaneously in a final year, one tutor cannot repair four and somebody has to choose which two matter.

What we will describe honestly is the shape of progress. At four weeks, a diagnosis and one visible procedural change. At one term, behaviour before numbers: questions started rather than stared at, working written down, plans made before essays, units checked without prompting. Often a test returns with the same mark and a different pattern of errors, which is real movement that looks like none and is where families most often lose their nerve.

Over a full examination cycle most students who attend, do the work between sessions and have a reasonable tutor move meaningfully; some move a great deal; a few do not move at all, usually for reasons that are not academic. The IB home tuition in Cumballa Hill that works is attached to a course the child is still turning up to and engaging with, because a tutor supplements school teaching rather than replacing it. A family searching for the best IB tutor in Cumballa Hill is, in the end, looking for a fit rather than a ranking, and nobody can rank a tutor across subjects and children.

sections.heading: Booking IB Gram home tuition in Cumballa Hill, Mumbai
paragraphs: Send the brief: year and programme, subject and level or tier, school, and what is going wrong in your own words. Send one per child. Add the evenings that are genuinely free rather than theoretically free, because that single line decides whether a good match survives past November. A slot colliding with a sport every other week produces a tutor who seems unreliable and a child who is never ready, and it is the most common avoidable failure on this hill.

Bring two things to the discovery call: the most recent report including the comments you would rather not share, and one piece of marked work where marks were lost rather than earned. A tutor working from an edited picture spends the first fortnight rediscovering what you already knew. Ask the tutor to react to the marked work while you listen, and notice whether they name a teaching move or describe a feeling.

Before the first lesson three practical things get settled. Building entry for a recurring weekly visitor, since a tutor negotiating at the desk burns part of every hour. A fixed room and a cleared table, which matters in a flat where the dining table is the family's evening centre. And a per-session figure in writing with the cancellation terms attached, agreed directly with the tutor rather than left to be discovered.

The honest summary of what you get and do not get. You get verified profiles matched to a board and a level, a written reason for each, a free discovery call, a dated review page, replacement whenever you ask and no lock-in. You do not get a promised grade, a ranking, or a claim that any individual is the strongest tutor available. What an IB tutor Mumbai families actually need is the right person for one child, one board and one year, and on a hill where two boards often share one flat that usually means two matches and one carefully protected timetable.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram already have tutors working on this hill?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects, usually yes, because tutors teaching here tend to hold several slots across Cumballa Hill, Kemps Corner, Breach Candy and Tardeo and can add one more without a new journey. For a scarce Higher Level combination or a less commonly taught language the answer is sometimes no, and then we either spend a few days shortlisting properly or propose weekly online lessons with the right specialist elsewhere. What we will not do is send a nearby approximation and let you find the mismatch in week three.

faqs.question: What do you need from me in the first message?
faqs.answer: Six items, and the whole thing fits in a short paragraph: the child's year and programme, the subject and level or tier, the school, what is going wrong in your own words, which evenings are genuinely free, and whether lessons should be in the flat or online. Each missing item costs a round of messages, and the evenings question is the one most often left out and the one that most often sinks a good match later. If you have a marked script, attach it.

faqs.question: Can both children be matched at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, as two briefs and two shortlists rather than one combined request. We usually suggest settling the child closer to an examination first, confirming that slot, then adding the second a few weeks later. Starting both in the same week tends to produce two half-attended arrangements and an overloaded evening, especially when one child is on the Diploma Programme and the other on the Cambridge route. Once both are running, we keep one review conversation covering both so you are not repeating yourself.

faqs.question: Is there a fee to get a shortlist or take the call?
faqs.answer: No. The brief, the shortlist and the discovery call cost nothing, and nothing is payable until you have agreed to a specific tutor for a specific slot. There is no joining fee, no minimum term and no notice period, which is a design decision rather than a courtesy: a parent who feels locked in stays quiet about a poor match for a term and the student loses the term. Payment terms themselves are agreed directly with the tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Who do I pay, and when?
faqs.answer: You agree terms with the tutor directly, in writing, before the first lesson. We will not publish figures because the honest range is too wide to inform anything and a printed number becomes an anchor rather than a guide. What we do insist on is that the arrangement is explicit before teaching starts: the per-session figure, how many sessions are being booked at a time, and what a cancellation at a day's notice costs on either side. Ambiguity there is the most common source of friction we see.

faqs.question: Will the tutor's travel be reflected in what we pay?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, indirectly, which is part of why we match locally. A tutor crossing Mumbai is charging for the hour lost in traffic as well as the hour taught, so a tutor already teaching in Tardeo or Kemps Corner is typically both cheaper and more reliable than a stronger profile from the Western Suburbs. Where a scarce specialist genuinely has to come from a distance, weekly online lessons remove the travel component entirely and usually cost less for the same teaching.

faqs.question: How do we handle building entry for a weekly visitor?
faqs.answer: It is set up once as a recurring entry rather than a fresh request each week. Lessons here happen inside the flat, and a tutor waiting at the desk while security calls upstairs loses a real part of a one-hour session. So before the first visit we confirm how your building clears a repeat visitor and whether anything is needed from you each time, and brief the tutor on that procedure. It also means an unplanned extra session before a mock needs a day's notice rather than an hour's.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of a term, or during examination leave?
faqs.answer: Whatever you decide at the review, which is why the review has a date. Examination leave in spring is the natural moment for a short intensive block rather than a weekly hour, because the school timetable empties and a tutor can run longer sessions on consecutive days. Some families pause instead, which is fine and does not cost anything. What we ask is that the decision is made at a review point rather than by sessions quietly not being booked, since a lapsed arrangement is hard to restart.

faqs.question: Can we pause for the monsoon or a long holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is common. There is no minimum term and no penalty for pausing, though we would flag one practical risk: a good tutor's slot does not stay empty for six weeks, so a long pause may mean a different time or a different tutor on return. Where continuity matters, a shorter online session through the break often holds the slot and the habit for less money than a full lesson. Decide it at a review rather than letting bookings simply stop.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Extended Essay and internal assessments?

Multi-subject briefs are the other place we push back. A single tutor who claims eight subjects across both boards is overstating, and nobody covers all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dadar families might collectively ask for. Related subjects pair naturally: Maths with Physics, History with English, Chemistry with Biology. Across distant subjects, depth falls away quickly. We will usually suggest starting with the priority subject for a month, then adding a second tutor rather than stretching the first, and we will say which subject we think the priority is and why.

Underneath subject choice sits structure, which a good tutor raises unasked. The HL and SL split in the Diploma Programme sets workload as well as difficulty, and the IGCSE Core and Extended tier decision does the same thing earlier. Each DP subject carries its own internal assessment, and in DP2 those drafts cluster with the Extended Essay and the TOK essay. sections.heading: Why Dadar changes who we can send
paragraphs: Dadar is where the Western and Central lines cross, which makes it the single easiest address in Mumbai for a tutor to reach from anywhere. Tutors accept Dadar slots they would refuse elsewhere, and that one fact reshapes the service here. A specialist in Andheri, Ghatkopar or Chembur who would never commit to a weekly evening in a less connected locality will commit to one at Dadar (Western & Central), because the journey is a train ride with a known duration rather than a nightly gamble on traffic.

Our coverage from here extends through Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga and Prabhadevi, and tutors who take a Dadar slot often add a second family in one of those within a few weeks. That clustering is what makes a weekly slot durable. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, and a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres while still losing much of their evening to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, so the advantage here belongs specifically to rail. When you ask a shortlisted tutor how they will travel, treat by train as a better answer than a short drive.

Parents searching IB tutors near me Dadar sometimes assume they should restrict themselves to tutors living within a kilometre. Here that would narrow the pool for no gain. The question that actually predicts a durable slot is not distance but journey type and position in the tutor's evening, and we put both on the profile. An IB home tutor in Dadar arriving on the Central Line at 5.45pm for a 6pm start is a more reliable arrangement than a neighbour who drives in from Prabhadevi after two other families.

sections.heading: Fitting home tuition around the Mumbai school week
paragraphs: Children from this area attend Don Bosco International School and JBCN International School, Parel, with Ryan Global School at Worli and the wider island options in Fort and Cuffe Parade also within reach. IB Gram has no relationship with any of them. They matter because their calendars decide when a weekly slot needs to flex, and because Dadar children tend to have unusually full weeks: a hub location means short school commutes and therefore more co-curriculars squeezed into the evenings.

Three points in the Mumbai, Maharashtra school year reliably disturb an arrangement. School examination weeks, when families want to either pause or double up and neither is usually right. The mid-year stretch when internal assessment drafts arrive across subjects at once, which is the one window where a second weekly session genuinely earns its place. And the monsoon, when a travelling tutor is the first thing to cancel and an online fallback saves the week rather than losing it. We ask about all three at the start so the arrangement is built to survive them.

The commonest scheduling error is booking around the school day instead of around the child. A 7.30pm start after school, a commute and a sports session produces an hour of poor attention, and the tutor gets blamed for it. Where late is the only option, shorter and more frequent beats longer and later. We say this on the call even when it means a smaller booking, because the alternative is a family cancelling in week six and concluding that home tuition in Dadar does not work when what did not work was the hour it was placed in.

sections.heading: Does home tuition in Dadar ever need to go online?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and switching for a few weeks is the most common adjustment we make. Home sessions are the lead service because a tutor in the room sees the exercise book, the school's annotations and the moment a student's attention goes, none of which reaches a screen reliably. But a term is long, and weeks arrive when nobody should be travelling: a monsoon evening, illness in the flat, a school trip, an examination fortnight when the student is at home all day anyway. Moving those weeks online keeps the habit instead of breaking it.

A permanent switch to an IB online tutor in Dadar makes sense in fewer cases here than elsewhere, precisely because the rail interchange means good tutors will travel. The two situations that still justify it are genuine scarcity, such as a less commonly taught language or an unusual Higher Level option with no specialist in the city, and a student old enough to work independently whose family would rather have the better tutor on a screen than the adequate one in the room. Both are legitimate, and neither should be the default.

What we will not do is move you online because staffing a home slot turned out to be awkward, and if a shortlist arrives online-only you should ask directly why. Hybrid, where it is chosen deliberately, works well: one session in the flat for teaching that needs a shared page, one shorter online session for marking review or a check before an internal assessment deadline. The test of whether hybrid is working is what the student does between the two sessions. If the answer is nothing, the second session is filling time.

sections.heading: Are you the first or the last family on the tutor's evening?
paragraphs: This is the question nobody asks and it predicts more than most parents would guess. A tutor with a good route through Dadar, Matunga and Prabhadevi may teach three families in an evening, and the third hour is not the same hour as the first. Fatigue is real, arrival time slips as the evening accumulates, and the last family absorbs every delay from the two before them. None of that makes the tutor dishonest. It makes position on the route a scheduling fact worth knowing before you agree a time.

The hub position cuts both ways here. Because Dadar is easy to reach, tutors build denser evenings than they would elsewhere, which is exactly what makes the pool wide and also what makes the 8pm slot risky. If your child works best early, say so and accept a 4.30pm or weekend morning slot in exchange for being first. If late is unavoidable, ask the tutor directly how many families precede you and whether they are all in this area. Three nearby families is a route; one in Bandra and one in Chembur before you is a sequence of gambles.

The same logic governs what to do when sessions start arriving late. One late arrival is weather. A pattern is a structural problem with the route, and the fix is a different slot or a tutor with a shorter evening, not a conversation about reliability. Tell us at the review and we will say which of the two it looks like. This is also why we ask for slot flexibility in the brief: a family who can move to Thursday at 5pm can often be placed first on a route, and first on the route is the most underrated thing you can negotiate for in IB Gram home tuition in Dadar.

sections.heading: No lock-in, no grade guarantees, and what that means
paragraphs: There is no minimum term, no joining fee and no notice period. You can stop after one session, and some families do once they discover the problem was not the one they described. What is reasonable to expect is smaller and checkable. At four weeks a tutor should be able to tell you what the diagnosis found, which two or three things they prioritised, what your child can now do that they could not in week one, and what remains outstanding. At one term, foundation gaps should have stopped being the reason marks are lost. School assessments in the targeted subject often move in the second term rather than the first, because the early gains sit in technique while tests reward coverage. Across a full examination cycle, the honest claim is that technique stops costing marks.

When a tutor is not working out, the mechanism is short. Tell us what happens in the room, in specifics. Sometimes the answer is a change of approach and we will ask the tutor for it. When it is a change of person, we return to the shortlist, arrange fresh discovery calls, and you choose again exactly as before. We would much rather replace a tutor in week three than hear in month four that a family quietly stopped a term they had paid for. faqs.question: Does IB Gram serve Dadar, and how quickly?

faqs.answer: The same one each week, and quieter matters more than larger. What is needed is a surface wide enough for a paper and a textbook side by side, a chair at a sensible height, and a boundary between the lesson and the rest of the household. We ask about this in the brief rather than discovering it in session one, because it changes which tutors we shortlist: some work well in a busy flat and some need a closed door. faqs.question: What exactly do I get after sending a brief?
faqs.answer: Either two or three verified profiles, or an honest timeline if the request is hard to staff. Each profile names the board and level that tutor currently teaches, the subjects they take and decline, where they travel from and how. Profiles arrive unordered because we do not rank tutors. You then take a free discovery call with each, with your child present if they will join. If none of them suit, say what did not fit and we shortlist again at no cost. faqs.question: Is there a minimum commitment or a lock-in period?
faqs.answer: No. There is no minimum number of sessions, no joining fee and no notice period to work out. You can stop after one session. The review we run at two to four weeks exists partly to make an early conversation easy, because parents are often reluctant to raise a mismatch with a tutor they chose themselves. Telling us in week three costs nothing and more often ends in a change of approach than a change of person. Hearing in month four that a family stopped quietly is the outcome we are trying to avoid.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Somebody should be in the flat, and for younger children a parent present for the first session is worth arranging. Ten minutes of your time at the start of session one is the highest-value ten minutes in the whole arrangement, because what worries you and what your child reports usually differ and the tutor needs both versions before planning. After that most families settle into being around rather than in the room. We ask who will be at home in the brief because it genuinely changes which tutors we shortlist.

faqs.question: What happens when a session is missed or runs late?
faqs.answer: Scheduling sits between you and the tutor, so a one-off clash is rearranged directly and most tutors are flexible about it. What we want to hear about is a pattern. Repeated late arrivals usually mean the tutor's evening route is too dense or your slot sits too late in it, and the fix is a different time or a tutor with a shorter evening rather than a conversation about reliability. Raise it at the review and we will tell you which of the two the pattern looks like, based on where you sit on their route.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay or an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor can challenge a research question that is too broad, ask what the data or evidence will look like before work begins, insist the process record is kept as the work happens rather than reconstructed later, and make the student rehearse their argument aloud. A tutor cannot write, edit or supply any part of it, and one willing to do so creates an academic honesty problem rather than solving an academic one. Ask each shortlisted tutor where they draw that line before lessons start.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Dadar depend on?
faqs.answer: Four things: the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, the travel involved, and the length and frequency of sessions. We do not publish a price list, because one figure would be wrong for most families reading this page and quoting it would mean inventing it. faqs.question: How is this different from a tuition class near the station?
faqs.answer: A class teaches a syllabus at a fixed pace to whoever enrolled. Home tuition teaches one student at the pace their own gaps require, and for IB and IGCSE students the difference shows up most on internal assessments and command terms, which are individual pieces of work and cannot be taught to a room. Classes can be the better choice when a student is broadly fine and wants structured practice with other people. They are a poor choice when the problem is specific, which is what most parents are describing when they contact us.

faqs.question: Can we start with one subject and add another later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and starting with one is usually wiser. A single subject for the first month tells you whether the arrangement works before you commit two evenings a week to it. Adding a second subject later often means a second tutor, because genuine depth across distant subjects is rare and a tutor claiming everything is overstating. Send a fresh brief for the new subject and we will shortlist against it while taking your existing slot into account, so the two do not land in the same crowded part of the week.

faqs.answer: Say so and we shortlist again, at no cost. It is part of the process rather than an exception. What helps is saying specifically what did not fit, because the reason is usually actionable: too far, wrong level experience, not available at the time you need, or a manner your child would not open up to. Where the subject is genuinely scarce we will also tell you honestly whether a third shortlist is likely to look different.

That is a request you can make of an IB home tutor in Dahisar at the start rather than hoping it emerges, and it is one of the few things tuition does better than anything else.

The practical consequence for your timing is that this is a seasonal market. sections.heading: Does IB Gram arrange home tuition, online lessons, or both in Dahisar?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and the lead service, and most families here want exactly that. The reason is not preference but mechanics: a tutor in the room supervises the practice, sees the folder with its unmarked worksheets, and corrects an error in the second it appears. For a student below the senior years, those three things are most of the benefit, and they do not travel well over video however good the connection is.

Online is arranged in three situations and we will recommend it rather than wait to be asked. When the right specialist for a scarce subject lives elsewhere in Mumbai. When the useful work in a final year is marked past papers and feedback, which needs no one in the room. And when the only workable slot sits in an hour no tutor can reliably travel through, which in April along the Western Express Highway is a real constraint rather than an excuse.

Online is the wrong choice for a student who cannot yet work alone for twenty minutes, and we say so even when agreeing would be easier. It is also the wrong choice for the first two or three diagnostic sessions in any year group, since telling a skill problem apart from a content problem needs a tutor watching a student write. Families who book IB home tuition in Dahisar for the diagnosis and move to a hybrid later get the best of both and usually pay the same.

The hybrid that holds through a full academic year here is one in-person visit a week plus a shorter online session placed in the worst travel hour. It keeps supervision where it matters and removes the fragility from the harder evening. Whichever arrangement you choose, the terms are the same: no lock-in, no minimum number of sessions, and a written review at two to four weeks that tells you whether it is working.

sections.heading: What a verified IB Gram profile means, and what it does not
paragraphs: Verified means four things have been checked before a profile reaches you: government photo identity confirmed, qualification documents sighted rather than claimed, a subject-level conversation held with someone who knows the programme, and teaching or tutoring history checked where it exists. A profile also states the programme, the level and the board the tutor has actually taught, which is the single most useful line on it and the one most services leave vague.

What verification does not mean is that we have predicted fit. No screening process anywhere can tell you whether this adult will get your fourteen-year-old to write six lines of method where she currently writes three. That is why you receive two or three profiles and a free discovery call with each, and why we treat the call as the real selection step rather than a formality before an invoice. Fit is decided by you, on the phone, in about ten minutes.

There are checks that remain yours and we would rather name them than imply we have covered everything. Keep lessons in a shared room with the door open and an adult somewhere in the flat; a professional tutor usually suggests this before a parent does. Ask what will be set between sessions and who marks it. And ask, before the first lesson, what document you will receive after four weeks, because a tutor who cannot describe it in advance is unlikely to produce it later.

Be wary of any tutor, on our platform or anywhere else, who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a percentage of students who improved. We do not guarantee grades and we publish no success rate, because an honest figure would have to separate the tutor's contribution from the school's teaching, the student's own work between sessions and the level she was entered at. Nobody runs that analysis, which makes every published number of that kind a marketing decision.

sections.heading: The review every two to four weeks: what happens if it is not working?
paragraphs: You tell us, and we replace the tutor at no switching cost and without asking you to make the case twice. That is the whole answer, and the review exists so that the question gets asked at a sensible point rather than drifting for a term. At two to four weeks the tutor should have produced a written note naming two or three specific weaknesses, the evidence behind the judgement, what has been set and marked, and what the next month will target.

Read that note against what you were told in the first session. If week one said the problem was unstructured written answers and the four-week note talks about growing confidence and topics covered, the original diagnosis has quietly been dropped. That drift is the most common failure in tuition anywhere and it is invisible unless the first diagnosis was written down, which is exactly why we ask for it in writing rather than over a phone call.

Replacements are routine rather than dramatic, and specificity makes them work. "Explains clearly but never sets anything between sessions" leads to a different second profile than "she has gone quiet and stopped asking questions". Most changed matches are about pace or personality rather than subject knowledge, most second matches hold, and nobody involved treats the request as a complaint about the first tutor. A tutor who is wrong for your child may be the right tutor for the family two buildings away.

Stopping altogether is also a legitimate outcome of the review and we would rather you did it than continue out of politeness. If the note concludes that the real constraint is exhaustion from a long school day, a subject combination the student cannot sustain, or a timetable with no room in it, then more hours will not help and we will say so. Families who stop after a month because the review identified the real problem have used IB Gram home tuition in Dahisar correctly.

sections.heading: What IB Gram will not do, in Mumbai or anywhere
paragraphs: We will not promise a grade. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rate and we will not predict a score in a first conversation, because the school's teaching, the subject, the level and the student's own work between sessions each contribute more than a weekly hour does. A service that offers a number is offering certainty it cannot own, and the parents who are most reassured by it are the ones most likely to be disappointed in the examination season.

We will not write a student's internal assessment, exploration, essay or project, and we instruct tutors not to. A tutor may teach the subject, challenge a research question that is too broad, point out an unsupported claim and show what properly presented work looks like. A tutor who supplies data, drafts text or chooses a topic is putting the student's qualification at risk, and the risk sits with the student rather than with the tutor. Any tutor offering that should be reported to us.

We will not claim a relationship with a school. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, society or examination board named anywhere on this site, and we name schools only because their calendars shape the work. We also will not name an individual teacher at a named school, in a profile or in a conversation, however much it might reassure a parent that someone's child's teacher is on the list.

And we will not sell you something we cannot fill. If the right tutor for your brief does not exist within reach of Dahisar this term, the honest answer is an online specialist, a weekend slot, a wait, or a referral back to the school, and you will get whichever applies. Parents who search "best IB tutor in Dahisar" are often expecting a pitch; what they get is a shortlist of two or three with the weaknesses of each stated out loud.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge or any Mumbai school?

If any tutoring service in Mumbai implies an arrangement with a named school or board, ask them to show it in writing, and treat the reaction as the answer.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a tutor after we send the brief?
faqs.answer: Usually a few days for mathematics, the sciences or language and literature in this catchment, and longer for a scarce subject or an awkward slot. The two things that slow it down most are a vague brief and an evening nobody can reach, which is why we ask for the marked work and the building details up front. If a subject genuinely cannot be filled locally this term, you will hear that rather than wait a fortnight for a weak profile, and we will put the online and weekend options in front of you instead.

faqs.question: What if we have to miss a week, or the tutor cannot come home that evening?
faqs.answer: Agree the cancellation arrangement with the tutor before the first session; it takes a minute and prevents most disputes. Reasonable practice is notice on both sides where possible, a rescheduled slot rather than a lost session, and an online substitute when travel collapses, which during the worst April weeks is a sensible default rather than a failure. Examination weeks, school trips and family travel are all ordinary reasons to pause. There is no minimum number of sessions, so a pause costs nothing except the slot, which the tutor may fill.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, at any point, with no switching fee and no requirement to justify the request twice. Three or four sessions is a fair point to judge, because by then a written diagnosis should exist and you can see whether work is being set and marked. Most changes are about pace or personality rather than knowledge, most second matches hold, and nobody treats the request as a complaint.

faqs.question: Do you cover Mira Road, Borivali East and Borivali West too?

Mira Road sits across the municipal boundary and the weekday evening crossing takes longer than the distance suggests, so Mira Road households are usually matched with a tutor already working that side. faqs.question: Can an IB Gram tutor help with an internal assessment or exploration?

We do not guarantee grades and publish no success rate, because the school's teaching, the level, the subject and the student's own work between sessions each matter more than the weekly hour. You can stop after one session, pause for an examination fortnight, move to a weekend slot when the highway gets difficult in April, or change tutors, and none of those requires a negotiation. sections.heading: IB Gram home tuition in Fort: the brief, the shortlist, the call
paragraphs: A brief from Fort arrives into a market where supply is the binding constraint, so the sequence we run is designed around capacity rather than around persuasion. You send a brief. We check who in the verified pool can teach that exact course and level, who has a slot that matches yours, and who is not already carrying too many students at that level in the same cohort. You read two or three profiles. You take a free discovery call. You approve a tutor, and the first lesson is scheduled.

The third check in that list is unusual and we think it is the most important one in this locality. The tutoring demand in these few streets comes largely from one school's IGCSE and IB Diploma Programme (DP) students, so the obvious tutors are approached by many families in the same term. Preparation is finite. A tutor reading mark schemes and marked scripts for several students at the same level distributes the same work across all of them, and the newest student receives the least of it. So we will decline to add you to a saturated tutor's list and say why, rather than place you and let the thinness show up in February.

What a brief needs is four lines. The exact course and level. What the last marked piece of work showed. The lesson address with the building and nearest cross street, plus the weekday evening you can hold. And who will be at the flat when the tutor arrives. Nothing is prepaid to us at any point, there is no registration charge, and your phone number is not circulated to a pool of tutors, which is why you receive a short list rather than several unsolicited calls. Our internal pool reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, and every IB Gram home tuition in Fort shortlist is narrowed down from it.

After approval the arrangement runs between you and the tutor: the timing, the rescheduling, the payment. We stay in it for the review, which is one question every two to four weeks, and for the replacement if the answer is unsatisfactory. There is no notice period because there is no contract to serve notice on, and an IB Gram home tutor in Fort can be replaced in a few days.

sections.heading: Which programmes and levels we can fill from a Fort brief
paragraphs: We match across all three International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes and both IGCSE routes, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, and in these streets the requests cluster heavily at two points. Years 9 to 11 on the IGCSE route, and DP1 or DP2. Primary Years Programme (PYP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP) briefs arrive too, but in smaller numbers, which matters because it affects how quickly we can fill them.

Honest availability by level, because guessing wastes your term. Across the common Diploma subjects at Standard Level (SL) and the main IGCSE sciences, mathematics and languages, we can usually fill a Fort brief within a week. Higher Level (HL) requests with a specific topic focus take longer. Uncommon languages, MYP Arts and Design, and anything needing a weekday slot before six in the evening are the hardest, because most capable tutors are teaching in a school at that hour somewhere in Mumbai.

The level distinction that costs families the most here is the IGCSE to Diploma bridge. IGCSE rewards coverage and accuracy against a defined syllabus with Core and Extended tiers; the Diploma rewards independent production, with Internal Assessment (IA) marked against published criteria, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) on top. A student entering DP1 in August often needs study-habit work rather than subject content for the first month, and a tutor who starts on syllabus material misses that window entirely.

What we will not do is advise on which subjects or which levels your child should take. That decision needs someone with the whole student in front of them, which means your school's coordinator rather than any tutor or platform. A tutor can give you an informed read on one subject's demands, and we will say clearly when a question sits outside what a tutor should answer. Board structures and assessment arrangements are revised on each board's own cycle, so treat your school's current documents as the authority.

sections.heading: What happens when the right subject tutor has no free slot?
paragraphs: We tell you, and then we give you four options rather than quietly sending someone less suitable. This situation is common in Fort because the popular evening slots across the cohort are committed early, often by late August, and a family enquiring in October is choosing from what remains. Pretending otherwise is how a parent ends up with a competent tutor on an impossible Monday at five-thirty.

Option one: move the slot. A Saturday morning or a later weekday start frequently opens up the exact specialist you wanted, and in this locality a protected weekend slot outlasts a contested weekday evening through the January crunch. Option two: take an online specialist for the same subject, which widens the pool beyond South Mumbai entirely and is the right answer when the requirement is narrow. Option three: a different verified tutor with capacity, which is often better than it sounds, because a tutor with room to prepare properly beats a celebrated one carrying too many students.

Option four is to wait, and sometimes it is correct. If the request is a single HL subject and the term is quiet, waiting three weeks for the right person is a better trade than paying for six lessons that address the wrong gap. We will say when we think waiting is the right call, which costs us the booking and is the advice we would want.

What makes any of these options work is a brief naming the component rather than the subject. "DP Economics, loses marks on the data response and draws no diagrams" can be matched against a technique specialist, a weekend slot or an online tutor with equal confidence. "Economics help" can only be matched against general availability. The all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Fort families keep running for years almost always started from a brief at that level of specificity, because it let us solve the scheduling problem without compromising the match. An all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Fort with a free Saturday is often a better answer than a saturated weekday specialist.

sections.heading: Does IB Gram cover Fort, Colaba and Mazgaon in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Yes, and a tutor matched to a Fort brief commonly works across all three plus Churchgate, sometimes in the same evening. The Fort heritage precinct sits between CSMT and Churchgate, so the practical catchment is defined by walking distance from a platform: Churchgate is a short walk or one stop, Colaba is walkable in good weather, and Mazgaon is close by road on the eastern side. A small area with an unusual amount of international-curriculum demand packed into it.

The tutor supply is wider than the catchment because two railway networks land here. A tutor on the Western Line comes to Churchgate, a tutor on the Central or Harbour Line comes to CSMT, and either walks the rest. That is the opposite of the usual South Mumbai problem, where road matching makes a tutor from the suburbs unreliable for a weekday evening. We still prefer a tutor who travels by train and we say so on the profile, because a car arriving in the evening peak is the part of the arrangement that breaks first.

Two Fort particulars affect scheduling and are worth putting in the brief. Parking near the older buildings is genuinely difficult, so a tutor who drives may need a longer buffer and will often prefer a later start. And several of the residential buildings here are heritage structures where the entrance, the stairs and the visitor desk all work differently from a modern tower, so tell us the building and which entrance to use rather than assuming it will be obvious at seven in the evening.

Because the precinct mixes offices and residences, a number of tutors who teach here already have reason to be in these streets during the day, which makes an early-evening slot practical without a special journey. Home tuition across this part of Mumbai is easier to sustain for that reason, and it is one of the few places in the city where asking for six o'clock on a Tuesday is not optimistic. sections.heading: One Fort cohort, many briefs, and how we allocate tutors
paragraphs: Cathedral and John Connon School is in Fort, and its IGCSE and IB DP students make up most of the tutoring demand in these few streets. B.D. A concentrated cohort creates an allocation problem that a city-wide platform can ignore and we cannot. If several families from the same class ask for the same subject in the same month, placing them all with the obvious tutor degrades every one of those arrangements. So we cap how many students one tutor carries at a single level within a cohort, and when the cap is reached we offer a different verified profile, a different slot or an online specialist, and we explain which it is. If you know now that you will want a second weekly slot in January, say so when you first write to us and the tutor will hold the capacity. Ask in January and it will already be taken by someone who asked in August. This is the most useful scheduling advice we can give any family in these streets, and it costs nothing to act on.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online lessons and weekend slots in Fort, Mumbai
paragraphs: In-person home tuition is the service we lead with and the majority of what we arrange here, helped by the fact that the precinct is walkable from two station networks. A tutor arrives at a fixed weekly slot, the marked scripts come out on a table, and the visit carries its own discipline. For a family judging whether the arrangement is working, an in-person lesson also leaves more behind: a time of arrival, a tone of voice, and something written.

Online is the option we reach for when the subject is scarce or the calendar is tight. An IB online tutor in Fort can be a specialist anywhere in the country, which solves the narrow HL topic request and the uncommon language that this locality's own pool cannot. It also solves discretion, which some families in a small social circle care about, and it documents itself better than a visit does when the tutor keeps a shared running file.

Weekend in-person slots deserve more attention than they get here. Saturday mornings survive a term better than a contested weekday evening, especially from January, and they suit tutors who would otherwise be crossing the city at six. Many Fort arrangements end up as a Saturday morning lesson plus a short online session in the weeks a draft is due, which covers both the teaching and the moment a student is actually stuck.

What we do not do is place students in groups. There are good coaching centres in Mumbai running batches, and in a single-cohort market the request to share a tutor between two neighbours' children comes up often. We decline it, because a shared lesson teaches to the middle and short-changes both children, and because in a cohort this small the confidentiality questions are real. Two consecutive one-to-one slots at one address is a different matter and we arrange that regularly.

sections.heading: Confidentiality and verification: what we will and will not say
paragraphs: In a market where most clients attend the same school, confidentiality is an operational matter rather than a policy page. We will not tell you which other families we work with, which tutors teach which children, or how anybody else's arrangement is going, however much it would help you decide. If a platform offers you that information, consider what it says about yours. Your brief, your address and your child's marked work go to the tutor you approve and to nobody else.

We hold tutors to the same line. A tutor should not discuss another student's marks, drafts or diagnosis with you, and a tutor who volunteers that material is telling you what they say about your child elsewhere. In this cohort several tutors genuinely do teach more than one child in a class, which is unavoidable and manageable, and the test is whether they keep the conversations separate. Tell us if one does not.

Verification itself covers three things and no more: identity confirmed, claimed qualifications checked against documents, and subject competence tested in a conversation with somebody who knows the syllabus well enough to tell teaching from presenting. That third step is the real filter. Claiming DP Biology is easy; describing where marks leave a data-analysis question is not. Profiles carry levels, boards, recency, travel origin, available evenings and mode, and deliberately carry no rating, student count or testimonial, because those are the easiest things to manufacture.

Two prohibitions apply to every tutor on the platform. They do not touch assessed work: no drafting an IA, no writing an EE introduction, no producing a Design submission, because the consequences of academic misconduct land on the student. And they make no claims about outcomes. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate; IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success figures, and would want to hear about any tutor who tells you otherwise.

sections.heading: What happens if something goes wrong mid-term?
paragraphs: You tell us, in one sentence, and we act within a few days. That is the whole escalation path and it exists because the most expensive failure in private tutoring is not a bad tutor, it is a mediocre arrangement nobody reported. Parents are reluctant to complain about someone their child likes and who is unfailingly pleasant, so problems surface in month five that were visible in week four.

The three things that actually go wrong, and what each needs. Travel reliability: a slot that keeps moving, which needs either a different slot or a tutor whose commute is shorter, and which we treat as a quality failure rather than an inconvenience. Subject depth: the tutor is pleasant and the teaching is above or below the real difficulty, which needs a different person and a sharper brief. And rapport: nothing is wrong technically and your child has stopped speaking during lessons, which needs a replacement and no post-mortem. Telling us which of the three it is makes the second match far more accurate than the first.

What a replacement involves in practice. We send a fresh shortlist, usually within a few days for a common subject. Nothing is prepaid to us and nothing is owed to the outgoing tutor beyond lessons taught, so there is no financial reason to persist. Ask the outgoing tutor for their written notes, because a handover carrying the original diagnosis and a record of coverage saves the next person two sessions of rediscovery. This is the main reason we ask every tutor to put the session-one diagnosis in writing at the start.

There is one escalation we handle differently. If a tutor has discussed another family's child with you, implied a relationship with a school, offered to work on an assessed submission, or promised a specific grade, tell us and it is not a scheduling conversation. Those are the conditions on which a tutor stays on the platform. Every IB Gram home tuition in Fort arrangement rests on them, and we would rather lose a popular tutor than keep one who does any of the four.

sections.heading: The review cycle, the handover pack and our honest limits
paragraphs: The review is one question every two to four weeks for the first few months: is this working, and what would you change. It is asked rather than waited for. What we expect you to be able to answer at four weeks is what the diagnosis was, what has been covered and whether your child's written work looks different. Not a grade, because four weeks is too early for one and a tutor showing you a number has usually set the test themselves.

The handover pack is the document that makes everything else cheap to change: the session-one diagnosis in a sentence you could repeat to the class teacher, a running record of coverage, and the current next step with a reason. Ask for it at the start rather than when you need it. Families who keep it can change tutor in a week without losing ground, and families who do not effectively start again, which is why a tutor who keeps everything verbal has made themselves hard to replace in a way that benefits them rather than your child.

At one term the measure is a school-assessed script read against the mark scheme, and the thing to look for is a change in the kind of error rather than the size of the number. A student who has stopped losing easy technique marks and now loses only the hard discrimination marks has moved up, even on a flat percentage. Many families reduce frequency at this point, which is a good outcome, and the better tutors suggest it before we do.

The limits, stated here because a brand page is where parents look for them. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. We cannot make a student who does not want to be taught engage with anybody, we cannot compress two years of missing foundations into the weeks before an examination session, and we cannot promise the first match is the right one. We will also tell you when tutoring is the wrong intervention: if a timetable is already full, if the school's comments concern effort and deadlines rather than skill, or if a learning need needs a specialist rather than a subject tutor. We have given that answer in these streets and lost the enquiry.
